cdc-guide.short: Harvard Center on the Developing Child, 2014
cdc-guide.title: Enhancing and Practicing Executive Function Skills with Children from Infancy to Adolescence
cdc-guide.published: Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University

says.0-1: For 6 to 18 months: lap games with an expected surprise, hiding games, imitation and copying games, simple role play, fingerplays, and conversation about what the infant notices.
says.1-3: For 18 to 36 months: freeze dance and start and stop songs, song games with movements, Follow the Leader, physical challenges, conversation and storytelling with what will you do next, talk about feelings, matching and silly sorting, puzzles, and imaginary play the child directs.
says.3-5: For 3 to 5 years: imaginary play with play plans, storytelling and acting out, reading, movement to rhythm and song games, obstacle courses and balance, yoga poses with slow breathing, dancing fast then slow, freeze dance, sorting with a switched rule, opposites bingo, songs that add on, cooking with waiting, and puzzles.

cdc-guide-5-7.short: Harvard Center on the Developing Child, 2014 (5 to 7)
cdc-guide-5-7.title: Executive Function Activities for 5- to 7-year-olds
cdc-guide-5-7.published: Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University, activities guide

says.3-5: For 5 to 7 years: freeze dance, musical chairs, Red Light Green Light, Mother May I, What Time Is It Mr Fox, the Magic Word game, Simon Says and Do As I Say Not As I Do, copy games, call and response, songs that add on, Packing for a Picnic, Concentration, clapping rhythms, yoga, Guess My Rule and I Spy.

brain-play.short: Harvard Center on the Developing Child, 2022
brain-play.title: Brain-Building Through Play: Activities for Infants, Toddlers, and Children
brain-play.published: Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University, with the LEGO Foundation

says.0-1: For 6 and 9 months: peekaboo and hiding games, Trot Trot to Boston, Pat-a-Cake, Dickory Dean, Baby See Baby Do, taking turns dropping a toy with Boom, conversation games and fingerplays.
says.1-3: For 12 months to 3 years: Toddler See Toddler Do, exploring over cushions on the floor, pretend phone and chores, Dump and Fill, simple hide and seek, the three cup memory game, matching and sorting, active songs, freeze dance, Follow the Leader, counting, puzzles and Be the Narrator.
says.3-5: For 4 to 7 years: freeze dance with positions, Simon Says, Red Light Green Light, Duck Duck Goose, What Time Is It Mr Fox, I Spy, Opposites Bingo and Continue the Story.

serve-return.short: Harvard Center on the Developing Child, 2019
serve-return.title: 5 Steps for Brain-Building Serve and Return
serve-return.published: Center on the Developing Child at Harvard University

says.0-1: Notice the serve and share the child's focus, return it with support, name what the child sees or feels, take turns and wait, and practise endings and beginnings, with peekaboo as the example.
says.1-3: Notice the serve and share the child's focus, return it with support, name what the child sees or feels, take turns and wait, and practise endings and beginnings, with peekaboo as the example.

aap-play.title: The Power of Play: A Pediatric Role in Enhancing Development in Young Children

says.0-1: Play grows from social smiling into serve and return, peekaboo and pat-a-cake, and pediatricians promote reading aloud alongside play from birth.
says.1-3: Object play that becomes symbolic, foundational motor skills, turn taking, and scaffolding when an adult turns a puzzle piece to help.
says.3-5: Pretend and rule-bound social play, physical and rough-and-tumble play, and games whose rules children negotiate.

activities.title: Peekaboo Hands
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your chest, a parent flat on their back, and nothing in your hands.
steps: Lie back with your baby on your chest and cover your face with both hands.
Hold still for a slow count of three, then say "Boo!" and open your hands wide.
Stretch the count a little longer each time, and stop while they are still smiling.

activities.title: Where Did You Go
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 6 months who can grab, with the cloth on your face and never on theirs.
steps: Lie down with your baby beside you and drape a scarf or towel over your own face.
Say "Where did I go?" and wait for them to pull it off, or peek out yourself after a slow count of five.
Say "Here I am!" with a big grin, and go again for as long as they like.

activities.title: Under the Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 6 months and up who can reach, and a parent lying on the floor beside them.
steps: Put a cup upside down over a toy while your baby watches it vanish.
Ask "Where did it go?" and wait a slow breath before you touch the cup.
Lift it with a gasp, then put it back and let them do the lifting.

activities.title: Sock Puppet Chat
activities.blurb: Good for a parent flat on the sofa, one spare sock, and a baby who likes being talked to.
steps: Pull a sock over your hand, let it peek over your knee at your baby, and say hello in a squeaky voice.
Duck the puppet out of sight and wait, quiet, until your baby makes any sound at all.
Pop it up somewhere new to answer them, and let the chat go back and forth.

activities.title: Toy Comet
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months and up, both of you flat on your backs, with one toy and nowhere to be.
steps: Hold a toy about a forearm away from your baby's face until their eyes settle on it.
Drift it slowly to one side, stop, and wait for their eyes to catch up before you move again.
Change direction now and then, and stop when they look away.

activities.title: Cushion Tunnel
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months and up who watches hard, and a parent on the floor with one cushion.
steps: Stand a cushion up between you and your baby, and walk a toy slowly behind it.
Pause while it is out of sight, then bring it out the far side and say its name.
Once they look to the far side before it comes out, send it back out the way it went in.

activities.title: Where Your Eyes Go
activities.blurb: Good for a baby lying on your chest or beside you, looking around a room you are too tired to tidy.
steps: Watch your baby's eyes and look at whatever they land on, even if it is the ceiling.
Name it in a few warm words, like "the lamp, the yellow lamp", and keep looking at it with them.
Say nothing more until their eyes move, then follow them to the next thing.

activities.title: Babble Back
activities.blurb: Good for a chatty baby of about 3 months and up, and a parent who can talk but not get up.
steps: Wait for your baby to make any sound, then answer it as if it were a real sentence.
Stop, look at them, and give them a long gap to take their turn.
Keep the turns going, and let them end the conversation when they look away.

activities.title: The Missing Word
activities.blurb: Good for a song your baby has heard a hundred times, sung lying down with the lights low.
steps: Sing a song your baby knows well, slowly, looking at their face.
Stop right before the last word of a line, and hold the silence with your eyebrows up.
Wait for a wiggle, a kick or a look, then land the word with a big smile.

activities.title: Stop Start Lullaby
activities.blurb: Good for the slow minutes before sleep, with your baby on your chest and the lights down.
steps: Lie back with your baby on your chest and hum or sing a lullaby they know.
Stop in the middle of a line and go completely still, breathing slowly.
The moment they wiggle, coo or look up, start again from where you stopped.

activities.title: Copy Cat
activities.blurb: Good for face to face time from about 6 months, your baby on your chest or beside you, no toys needed.
steps: Copy your baby's face or sound one beat after they make it, a tongue out, a squeak, a frown.
Do it a few times, then make one new slow face of your own and hold it.
Wait, with the face on, for them to try it back.

activities.title: Piggy Pause
activities.blurb: Good for bare feet on your lap, a baby lying face up, and a parent who knows one rhyme.
steps: Sing this little piggy on your baby's toes, one toe for each pig, slowly.
At the last toe, stop and hold their foot still for a long count of three.
Then run your fingers up to their tummy on "wee wee wee" and start on the other foot.

activities.title: Round the Garden
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap with an open palm, and a parent whose hands still work after the day.
steps: Sing round and round the garden while your finger circles your baby's open palm.
On "one step, two step" creep your fingers up their arm, then freeze just under their chin.
Hold the freeze until they squirm, give one tiny tickle under the chin, and stop if they turn away.

activities.title: Who's in There
activities.blurb: Good for tummy time from about 5 months, you flat on the floor beside your baby, and a mirror in front.
steps: Lie on your tummy beside your baby and prop a mirror where you both appear in it.
Tap the baby in the mirror and say their name, then tap their real nose and say it again.
Make a slow face in the mirror and wait to see which of you they turn to.

activities.title: Ready Steady Raspberry
activities.blurb: Good for a bare tummy, a baby lying across your lap or beside you, and a parent with one breath left.
steps: Say "ready", wait, say "steady", wait longer, then "go" and blow a gentle raspberry on their tummy.
Blow until you say "stop", then lift your head and hold still for a count of two.
Go again only when they look at you or kick, and stretch the waits as they catch on.

activities.title: Baby Mind Reader
activities.blurb: Good for a grizzly or wriggly baby on your lap, and a parent who can talk softly but not much else.
steps: Watch your baby for a moment and say what they seem to want, like "you want that spoon".
Name the feeling too, in a calm voice, like "that noise made you jump".
Pause after each guess, give them a beat to answer, then help with the thing they wanted.

activities.title: Lamp Off, Lamp On
activities.blurb: Good for the sofa by a lamp at dusk, with your baby on your lap and your one free hand on the switch.
steps: Sit by a lamp you can reach, or point your phone torch at the ceiling, with your baby on your lap.
Say "off" slowly and switch it off, wait for them to look for it, then say "on" and bring it back.
Stretch the dark pause a little each time, and keep your voice soft the whole way.

activities.title: Where's Your Nose
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap looking up at you, and a parent with one finger's worth of energy.
steps: Ask "Where's your nose?" and wait a slow breath while you look at their face.
Touch their nose gently and say "nose", then do the same for ears, toes and tummy.
After a few rounds, ask "Where's my nose?" and move their hand to yours.

activities.title: Flat Out Story
activities.blurb: Good for lying on the bed with your baby beside you, one picture book, and no energy for the voices.
steps: Lie side by side and hold a picture book open above you both.
Point to one picture, name it, and wait until their eyes land on it before you turn or speak again.
If they look at something else on the page, name that instead and stay there.

activities.title: The Slow Fist
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months and up who grabs, and a parent with one working hand.
steps: Close your fist around a toy too big to swallow, a bit of it poking out, while your baby watches.
Ask "What's in there?" and open one finger at a time, as slowly as you can.
Let them pull your fingers open if they want to, and close up again for another go.

activities.title: Wiggly Sock
activities.blurb: Good for a parent flat on the rug, a baby of about 6 months sitting by their feet, and one bright sock.
steps: Lie on the rug with a sock on one foot and wiggle your toes until your baby watches.
Slide the sock foot under a blanket and ask "Where did the sock go?" in a whisper.
Wiggle it under the blanket, wait, and let them pull the blanket off to find it.

activities.title: Something Moves
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months and up on your chest, and a room where a fan or a curtain does the work.
steps: Lie back with your baby and find one thing that moves by itself, like a fan, a curtain or a shadow.
Turn so you both see it, and watch it together without a word until they look away.
When they look at it, say one soft thing about it, like "round and round", and go quiet again.

activities.title: Find My Face
activities.blurb: Good for tummy time from about 5 months, with you lying on your tummy too, nose to nose on the rug.
steps: Lie on your tummy facing your baby, a hand's length apart, and go quiet until they look away.
Say their name softly, once, and wait for their eyes to come back to your face.
When they find you, hold the look with a big slow smile, and tell them one thing about their day.

activities.title: Here You Go
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 9 months and up on your lap, and a parent who can hold out one hand.
steps: Hand your baby a toy, say "here you go", and let them have it for a while.
Hold out your open hand, say "my turn", and wait without grabbing, even if it takes a minute.
When they put it in your hand, say "thank you", then give it straight back with "your turn".

activities.title: Eyes on Me
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 6 months and up lying beside you, a toy in one hand and your face as the star.
steps: Lie face to face with your baby and hum while your face does slow silly things.
Now and then, wiggle a toy at the edge of their view for a second, then hide it again.
When their eyes stay on you instead of the toy, reward them with a huge grin and a kiss.

activities.title: Look Where I Look
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 9 months who sits, two toys on the rug, and a parent who can only move their head.
steps: Sit with your baby and put two toys on the floor in front of you both.
Turn your head to one toy, look hard at it, and say its name once.
Wait for their eyes to follow yours, then name it again and let them have it.

activities.title: Uh Oh Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months and up lying beside you, an empty cup, and a parent who can tip their head.
steps: Lie beside your baby, balance an empty cup on your forehead, and count a slow "one, two, three".
Tip your head away from your baby so the cup slides off onto the rug with a big "uh oh".
Put it back and count again, a little slower each time, and watch them brace before it falls.

activities.title: Snore and Wake
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who wants to close their eyes, and a baby of about 6 months sitting or lying beside them.
steps: Lie back on the rug, shut your eyes and snore loudly, with one hand resting against your baby.
The moment they touch you or make a sound, wake up with a slow surprised face and say "Oh, hello".
Smile, then yawn, close your eyes and snore again, giving them time to try once more.

activities.title: You Choose
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 6 months and up who reaches, on your lap or beside you, with two toys to hand.
steps: Hold up two toys, one in each hand, a little apart and well within reach.
Say "Which one?" and wait, without moving, until they look longer or reach for one.
Give them that one, name it, and put the other out of sight before you offer two again.

activities.title: What Was That
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your chest in the evening, with the house making its usual noises around you.
steps: Lie still with your baby and wait for a sound, like the kettle, a door or a dog outside.
Say "What was that?" and turn your head slowly toward it, so they turn too.
Name it in two or three words, then go quiet and wait for the next one together.

activities.title: Tug of Turns
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 6 months and up who grips, sitting on your lap, with a scarf or tea towel.
steps: Let your baby grab one end of a scarf while you hold the other.
Say "my turn" and give one gentle tug, then go loose and say "your turn".
Wait for their pull before you tug again, and let them win the scarf at the end.

activities.title: Peeking Tail
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 5 months who grabs but cannot yet find a fully hidden toy, lying beside you.
steps: Lay a cloth over a toy so a corner of it still peeks out, right where your baby can reach.
Ask "Where did it go?" and tap the peeking bit, then wait with your hands off.
When they pull the cloth, cheer softly, and cover a little more of the toy each time.

activities.title: Two Hands Full
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about a year with a toy in each hand, and a parent willing to wait.
steps: Wait until your baby has a toy in each hand, then hold out a third one they like.
Say nothing and count slowly to ten while they work out what to do.
Whatever they try, dropping one or reaching anyway, name it warmly and offer the new toy again.

activities.title: Empty Cup Tea
activities.blurb: Good for a baby of about 10 months and up on your lap, an empty cup, and a parent who can slurp.
steps: Lift an empty cup to your lips and drink loudly from it, with a big "ahh" at the end.
Hold the cup to your baby's lips for a pretend sip, then hand it over and wait.
Whatever they do with it, slurp along with them and say "cheers".

activities.title: Row Boat Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby on your lap, a song you both know, and a parent who can rock but not get up.
steps: Sit your baby on your lap facing you, hold their hands, and rock back and forth as you sing Row Your Boat.
Stop dead somewhere in the song, never the same place twice, hands still, and hold the quiet.
The moment they lean, pull or kick, rock on and finish the song.

activities.title: Pat a Cake Pause
activities.blurb: Good for a baby sitting facing you who already loves the rhyme, and hands that know it by heart.
steps: Sit face to face and chant Pat a Cake, patting your baby's palms with yours on every beat.
Before the big clap, open your hands wide and freeze for a slow breath.
Clap the moment their eyes come up to yours, and stretch the freeze a little next round.

activities.title: Trot to Boston
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who sits well on your knees, held under the arms, and a parent on a chair.
steps: Sit your baby on your knees facing you, hands firm under their arms, and bounce to Trot, Trot to Boston.
On the last line, part your knees so they dip a hand's width, held tight the whole way.
Slow the last line down a little each round and watch them brace before the dip.

activities.title: Two Cup Switch
activities.blurb: Good for the high chair tray and a baby from about 8 months who reaches for whatever you hide.
steps: Turn two cups upside down on the tray and tuck a toy under one while your baby watches.
Count a slow "one, two, three", then let them lift a cup and find it.
After a few wins, move the toy under the other cup in full view, count again, and watch where they reach.

activities.title: Drop and Tip
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby who drops everything, and a parent with a cup and nothing else.
steps: Hold a tall cup low in front of your baby and let them drop a block or a rolled sock in.
Shake it once so they hear it, ask "where did it go?" and wait for them to look at the cup.
Tip it slowly into their lap, hand the block back, and hold the cup a bit higher each round.

activities.title: Knock on Three
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby who flattens every tower, and a parent with cups to spare.
steps: Stack three or four cups while your baby watches, then hold their hands loosely in yours.
Count "one, two" slowly and let their hands go only on "three" so they can swipe.
Build again, and make the gap before "three" a touch longer each time.

activities.title: Ball Back
activities.blurb: Good for a baby sitting steady on the floor, or a crawler, and a parent sitting across from them.
steps: Sit on the floor facing your baby, legs wide to make a pen, and roll the ball slowly into their lap.
Hold out your hands and wait in silence until they push it back, or crawl over with it.
Say "my turn", roll it again, and let the waits get longer.

activities.title: Thank You Swap
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby who hands you things and wants them straight back.
steps: Hold out an open hand and wait until your baby puts the toy in it, then say "thank you".
Keep it one slow beat, offer it back, and let go only when their hand closes on it.
Add a second toy so they have to let go of one to take the other.

activities.title: Sock Drop
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap at the table, or a crawler who will go and fetch it.
steps: Hold a rolled sock at your baby's eye level, say "ready", and let it fall.
Look down at the floor together and ask "where did it go?" before you point.
Let them spot it, or crawl to it, then fetch it up and drop it again.

activities.title: Where's the Dog
activities.blurb: Good for one picture book, a baby on your lap, and the same page for the twentieth time.
steps: Open a picture book on your lap and tap one thing on the page, naming it as you tap.
Turn the page and back again, ask "where's the dog?" and wait before you point.
Name whatever they tap, even if it is not the dog, then ask again.

activities.title: Switch Boss
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your hip by the light switch as the room gets dark.
steps: Stand by the switch with your baby on your hip, flick the light on, and say "on".
Rest your hand on the switch and wait until they squeal, kick or stare at it, then flick it and say "off".
Say what they asked for as you do it, "you want it on", and switch only on their signal.

activities.title: Sock Fist
activities.blurb: Good for a baby from about 8 months who grabs, and a parent with two hands and one sock.
steps: Show your baby a scrunched sock, close your fist around it, and hold both fists out side by side.
Ask "which hand?" and count a slow two before you let them pick.
Open the fist they grab, whichever it is, and switch hands every round.

activities.title: Half Hidden
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby from about 6 months who reaches, a favourite toy and a tea towel.
steps: Set the toy in front of your baby and lay a cloth over half of it while they watch.
Ask "where did it go?" and wait for them to pull the cloth or grab the toy.
When that is easy, cover it completely, wait a slow breath, and ask again.

activities.title: Clap Back
activities.blurb: Good for a baby sitting facing you who is starting to clap or wave.
steps: Clap twice slowly in front of your baby, then hold still with your hands up and wait.
When they clap, or try to, clap back once and switch to a wave.
Whenever they start a move of their own, copy it exactly and let them lead for a while.

activities.title: Big Voice Tiny Voice
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap and a song they have heard a hundred times.
steps: Sing one line of a song they know in your biggest voice, arms wide.
Sing the next line in a whisper, leaning in close so they watch your mouth.
Keep flipping big and tiny, and flip early whenever their eyes come up to yours.

activities.title: Point and Name
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap in any room, from about 9 months when they start to follow a point.
steps: Point at one thing across the room and hold your arm there until your baby's eyes land on it.
Name it once, slowly, then look back at them and wait.
Now follow their look instead, and name whatever they stare at.

activities.title: Window Movers
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your hip at the window while dinner cooks or the day winds down.
steps: Stand at the window with your baby on your hip and wait, saying nothing, until something moves.
The moment they look, point and name it, "a bus", and follow it together until it is gone.
Go quiet again and wait for the next mover.

activities.title: Up Up Up Down
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby on your shins and a parent on the floor with their knees bent.
steps: Sit on the floor, knees bent, with your baby on your shins facing you and your hands under their arms.
Sing "up" on each slow lift of your knees, and "down" as you lower them in one go.
Change how many ups come before the down, and pause when they grin ahead of it.

activities.title: Ring Ring
activities.blurb: Good for a baby from about 9 months who babbles at your phone, in a high chair or on the floor.
steps: Hold your hand to your ear, say "ring ring, hello?", and chat to Grandma for a moment.
Hold your hand to their ear, say "it's for you", and wait for any sound at all.
Answer whatever they say, then pass the call back and forth.

activities.title: Shake and Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby, one cup, one rolled sock, and a parent who can hum.
steps: Drop a rolled sock in a cup, cover the top with your palm, and shake it in time as you sing.
Stop the shaking and the song halfway through a line, hold the cup still, and watch their face.
Start again the moment they look up or kick, then let them hold the cup and shake.

activities.title: Mirror Swap
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your lap in front of a mirror, from the age they smile at the baby in it.
steps: Sit with your baby on your lap facing a mirror and wave at the two of you in the glass.
Tap the glass and say "mirror baby", then tap their chest and say their name.
Make a slow funny face in the mirror and hold it until they turn to check the real you.

activities.title: Knee Tunnel
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler and a parent sitting on the floor with their knees up.
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees up to make a tunnel and put a toy on the far side.
As they crawl up, hold your hand flat in front of the tunnel as a gate and say "wait".
Say "go" and lift the gate, then make the next wait a touch longer.

activities.title: Echo Chat
activities.blurb: Good for a chatty baby in the high chair and a parent with no words left.
steps: Wait for your baby to make a sound, then say it back exactly, same pitch, same length.
Raise your eyebrows and wait, mouth closed, until they take the next turn.
After a few turns change one sound, "ba" to "bo", and see if they follow.

activities.title: Cushion Peek
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby on the rug, a big cushion, and a parent with one quiet "boo" left.
steps: Sit facing your baby and hold a big cushion up in front of your face.
Pop out on the left with a "boo", hide again, and pop out on the left once more.
Watch where their eyes go, then pop out on the right.

activities.title: Open Arms
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby of about 6 months and up who leans in for cuddles, and a parent who can wait.
steps: Sit facing your baby, hold out both arms, and ask "hug?" without moving closer.
Wait, still and smiling, until they lean, reach or wobble toward you.
Scoop them into a hug, set them back down, and hold out your arms again a little longer each time.

activities.title: Rattle Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby who grabs, two cups, one small toy, and a parent on the floor.
steps: Drop a toy too big to swallow into one of two cups, then cover both tops with your hands.
Shake each cup in turn so only one rattles, then set them down side by side.
Ask "which one?" and let them tip a cup over, then move the toy for the next go.

activities.title: Nose Beep
activities.blurb: Good for a baby from about 9 months who pokes your face, sitting on your lap or facing you.
steps: Press your own nose and say "beep", then press theirs and say "beep".
Lean in and wait until they poke your nose, and beep every single time they do.
After a while make your ear a new button that says "boing", and see which one they go for.

activities.title: Light Spot
activities.blurb: Good for a dim bedroom, a phone torch, and a baby on your lap who is nearly ready for sleep.
steps: Dim the room, shine your phone torch on the wall, and wait until your baby finds the spot.
Slide the spot slowly along the wall, then switch it off and ask "where did it go?"
Switch it on in a new place, and let them find it before you move it again.

activities.title: Hallway Hide
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler who follows you everywhere and a hallway with a doorway to duck behind.
steps: Sit at the end of the hallway and call your baby's name until they crawl to you.
When they arrive, scoot behind the doorframe out of sight and call again, softly.
Pop your head out when they get close, and hide a little further along next time.

activities.title: Rain Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a bath that is already happening, a sitting baby, and one cup.
steps: Fill a cup and hold it high over one of your baby's hands, pause, then pour a thin stream onto it.
Move the cup slowly over to the other hand and wait until they look up at the cup.
Pour the moment they look, and keep moving the rain to new spots.

activities.title: So Big
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby, from about 9 months, and a parent who can lift two little arms.
steps: Ask "how big is baby?" in a sing song voice, lift both their arms high and sing "so big".
Do it a few times, then ask the question and wait with your hands in your lap.
Cheer any lift, even one arm, then ask again with a longer wait.

activities.title: Splash Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a bath that is already happening, a sitting baby with a hand in reach, and some wet sleeves.
steps: Hold your baby's hands and pat the water together as you say "splash, splash, splash".
Say "stop" and lift their hands clear of the water, holding still for a slow count of two.
Say "splash" and start again, and let the stops get a little longer.

activities.title: Sound Around
activities.blurb: Good for a baby sitting steady on the rug, a parent who can shuffle around them, and no toys.
steps: Sit behind your baby to one side, just out of their view, and click your tongue softly once.
Wait until they turn and find your face, then smile and say their name.
Shuffle quietly to a new spot and click again, waiting a little longer each time.

activities.title: Tap Tap Turns
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting baby who bangs on everything, one upturned cup, and a parent sitting across from them.
steps: Turn a cup upside down between you and tap it twice with your fingers, then put your hands in your lap.
Wait, looking at your baby, until they tap or slap the cup themselves.
Answer with two taps of your own, and keep the turns going as long as they do.

activities.title: Ready Steady Fly
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who holds their head up, a spot clear of lampshades, and a parent with arms to spare.
steps: Hold your baby facing you with your hands firm around their chest and say a slow "ready, steady".
On "go" lift them slowly up to your shoulder height, then float them gently back down.
After a few rounds say the whole count in a whisper so they have to listen for the quiet "go".

activities.title: Song Stop Dance
activities.blurb: Good for a baby snug on your chest, a kitchen with room to turn, and a parent who sings badly.
steps: Hold your baby against your chest and sing any song while you sway and step around the room.
Stop singing in the middle of a line and freeze mid step for one slow breath.
Take a big loud breath and carry on exactly where the song left off.

activities.title: Doorway Boo
activities.blurb: Good for a baby sitting by a doorway, a parent who needs to stand, and the oldest joke that still works.
steps: Sit your baby on the floor an arm's length from a doorway and step behind the frame so they lose you.
Call "where did I go?" once, wait one slow breath, then lean out with a "boo".
Pop out low the next time, then high, so they have to hunt for where your face will come.

activities.title: Creep and Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler on the move, a cleared rug, and a parent whose knees can take a little creeping.
steps: Get on all fours behind your crawling baby and creep after them saying "creep, creep, creep".
Say "stop" and freeze like a statue for a slow count of three, however hard they stare at you.
Say "go" and creep on behind them, letting them pick the pace and the turns.

activities.title: Three Things Tour
activities.blurb: Good for a baby on your hip, a home with a kettle, a plant and a window, and a parent who likes to narrate.
steps: Carry your baby to three things in your home, and at each one stop, point and name it twice.
Walk the loop again and ask "where's the kettle?" a step before you reach it, then wait.
Point and name it the moment they look, and on the third loop name anything else they stare at.

activities.title: Last Word Bounce
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who holds their head up, a short rhyme you know by heart, and a parent with springy knees.
steps: Hold your baby against your chest and dip your knees in a gentle bounce on every beat of a short rhyme.
On the very last word stop dead and hold still with your mouth open.
Count two in your head, then start the rhyme from the top.

activities.title: Behind My Back
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who already grabs for toys, a favourite rattle, and a parent pacing the room anyway.
steps: Show your baby a toy, slide it behind your back and walk a slow circle around where they sit.
Ask "where did it go?" and bring it out on your left side with a big "there it is".
Next time bring it out on your right, and keep swapping sides so they look before they reach.

activities.title: Three Step Summit
activities.blurb: Good for a confident crawler, the bottom of the stairs, and a parent who will stay one step behind.
steps: Kneel on the floor behind your crawling baby at the bottom step, hands ready at their hips.
Count "one" as they climb the first step, and count each step after it, up to three.
At three say "top", lift them gently back down to the bottom and start the count again.

activities.title: Mirror Vanish
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who loves their own face, a hallway mirror, and a parent walking past it anyway.
steps: Stand in front of a mirror with your baby in your arms and say hello to the two of you.
Step sideways out of the mirror together, saying "gone" in a tiny voice, and wait one slow breath.
Slide back in with "there we are" and let them catch their own eyes before you go again.

activities.title: Copy the Crawler
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler in charge, a rug with nothing on it, and a parent happy to take orders.
steps: Get down beside your crawling baby and copy every move they make, crawl for crawl and pat for pat.
When they stop, you stop, and when they make a sound, you make it straight back.
After a few minutes do one new move yourself, like patting the floor, and wait to see if they copy you.

activities.title: Hallway Roller
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler who has found the hallway, a soft ball, and a parent who can crawl a few lengths.
steps: Sit with your baby at one end of the hallway and roll a ball slowly away from you both.
Say "go" and crawl beside them after it, naming the ball every time they look at it.
When they reach it, help them roll it back the other way and chase it home together.

activities.title: Sofa Boing
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who holds their head up, a sofa, and a parent whose thighs can take a few squats.
steps: Sit on the sofa with your baby held snug against your chest and go very still.
Say a long slow "boooo" and on "ing" stand up in one smooth move, then sit back down.
Stretch the "boooo" longer each round so they wait, eyes on you, for the "ing".

activities.title: Baby Says Go
activities.blurb: Good for a chatty baby, any room with a loop to walk, and a parent who would rather be told what to do.
steps: Hold your baby close and stand still, lips shut, until they make any sound at all.
The moment they do, say "go" and walk them briskly round the room, then stop dead.
Wait in silence again, and only their next squeak or babble starts you walking.

activities.title: There It Is
activities.blurb: Good for a window onto a street or garden, a baby who stares at things, and a parent who can stand a while.
steps: Carry your baby to the window and wait together for a bus, a bird or anything that moves.
When one appears, point and say "there it is", then follow it with your finger until it goes.
Say "gone" with a shrug, then go quiet and wait for the next one together.

activities.title: Sock Flight
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler, a rolled sock from the laundry pile, and a parent who can keep crawling after them.
steps: Roll a sock into a ball and throw it in a slow high arc so your baby's eyes can follow it down.
Say "where did it land?" and crawl beside them while they go and get it.
Land it somewhere new every time so they go to where it fell, not where it was before.

activities.title: Chair Tunnel
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler, one sturdy kitchen chair, and a parent who can get down on the floor.
steps: Set your baby at one side of a kitchen chair and lie down on the other side, holding the chair steady.
Call them through the tunnel under the seat and cheer when their head pops out your side.
Crawl round to the other side and call them back through, and let them take their time.

activities.title: Doorway March
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who holds their head up, a home with a few doorways, and a parent with a marching song.
steps: Hold your baby against your chest and march from room to room, stamping and singing any song.
Stop dead at every doorway, go silent for one breath, and whisper "door".
Stamp through with a loud "march" and sing on until the next doorway.

activities.title: Lights Off Tour
activities.blurb: Good for the evening, a baby who stares at lamps, and a parent walking from room to room anyway.
steps: Carry your baby into a room, point at the light switch and say "lights off", then stand still.
Flick it off, wait in the dark for one slow breath, and say "lights on" just before you flick it back.
Move to the next room and do it again, and let their hand help with the switch when they reach for it.

activities.title: Watch Me Wiggle
activities.blurb: Good for a baby propped up on the floor, a parent who needs to shake the day off, and no music at all.
steps: Sit your baby on the floor and dance right in front of them, as silly as you like, for as long as they watch.
The second their eyes leave you, freeze mid wiggle and go silent.
When they look back, burst into the dance again, so their looking is what keeps you going.

activities.title: Baby Steers
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who points or stares, any room, and a parent who can switch off and be driven.
steps: Carry your baby and walk only where they look or reach, saying "you want the lamp" as you go.
Stop at the thing, name it again, and let them touch it for as long as they like.
When their eyes move on, follow them to the next thing, and never pick the route yourself.

activities.title: Cushion Lap
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler of seven months and up, three sofa cushions, and a parent who can do laps of the rug.
steps: Lay three cushions on the floor and let your baby watch you tuck a toy under one of them.
Crawl one slow lap of the rug together, come back, ask "which one?" and let them lift a cushion.
Hide it under a different cushion each round, and cheer whether they find it or lift the wrong one.

activities.title: Teddy's Big Day
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who watches everything, a soft toy, and a parent who can act out a very small day.
steps: Carry your baby and a soft toy to the table, where teddy eats breakfast with loud munching.
Walk on to the sink where teddy washes his face, then to the sofa where teddy yawns and lies down.
Help your baby pat teddy goodnight, then wake him with a big stretch and start his day again.

activities.title: Slow Song Quick Song
activities.blurb: Good for a baby held close, a song you can sing two ways, and a parent who needs to get the blood moving.
steps: Hold your baby against your chest and sing a verse very slowly, swaying like a boat.
Sing the same verse quick and bright and take small quick steps around the room.
Switch between the two without warning, and watch their face catch the change.

activities.title: Which End
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler of eight months or so, a sofa, and a parent who can crouch behind an armrest.
steps: Sit your baby in front of the sofa and crouch behind one armrest, close enough to touch them.
Call "where am I?" and let them crawl round to find you, then celebrate loudly.
Hide behind the other armrest next time and see if they crawl to the new end or the old one.

activities.title: Chase the Spot
activities.blurb: Good for a dim evening, a phone torch, a baby lying or sitting on the floor, and a parent on their feet.
steps: Dim the room, turn on your phone torch and shine a spot on the wall where your baby can see it.
Walk slowly along the wall so the spot creeps with you, and keep it well away from their face.
Bring the spot down onto the floor by their hands and let them try to catch it.

activities.title: Tower Chase
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler who knocks things over, a few cups or blocks, and a parent who can build fast.
steps: Stack three cups an arm's length from your baby, naming each one as it goes on.
Say "ready, steady, crash" and let them knock it down, or knock it with them.
Build the next tower on their other side so they have to turn and travel to it.

activities.title: Page Walk
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who chews books, a picture book full of everyday things, and a parent on their feet.
steps: Carry your baby and a picture book, open a page and name one thing on it, like the cup.
Walk to a real cup in your home, tap it and say "cup" again, then tap the picture.
Turn the page and go and find the next thing, one page per trip.

activities.title: Hum Hunt
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who sits well, a cushion at their back just in case, and a parent who hums.
steps: Sit your baby on the floor with a cushion behind them and walk a slow circle around them, humming.
Stop right behind them, keep humming, and wait for them to turn and find you.
When their eyes land on you, sing their name and start the circle the other way.

activities.title: Listen Stops
activities.blurb: Good for a late evening, a sibling asleep, and a parent who needs a game played in whispers.
steps: Carry your baby slowly through the home and stop the moment you hear a sound, like the fridge or a tap.
Put a finger up, whisper "listen", and stay still until they turn towards it.
Whisper what it is, point at it, and walk on to find the next sound.

activities.title: Catch the Log
activities.blurb: Good for a crawler, a rug with room to roll, and a parent who would like to lie down but keep playing.
steps: Lie on your back beside your crawling baby and roll one slow turn away from them, saying "rolling".
Stop flat, call "come and get me", and wait until they crawl over and touch you.
Roll one more turn away each time they catch you, then let them climb on you as the prize.

activities.title: Slow Delivery
activities.blurb: Good for a baby who sits, a toy they want, and a parent who can crawl at the speed of a snail.
steps: Sit your baby on the floor, hold a toy they want an arm's length away, and get down on all fours.
Crawl it towards them at a snail's pace, saying "coming, coming", and pause twice on the way.
Say "now" and hand it over, and when they drop it, start another delivery from an arm's length away.

activities.title: Drop and Look
activities.blurb: Good for a baby in the dropping phase, a soft toy, and a parent who can squat twenty times.
steps: Hold your baby on your hip, hand them a soft toy, and let them drop it while you both watch it fall.
Say "uh oh" and wait, saying nothing more, until they look at you.
The moment they look, say "again", squat down to pick it up and hand it back.

activities.title: Cup Trio
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor, back against the sofa, three cups, and a kid who loves finding things.
steps: Turn three cups upside down in a row and tuck a toy under one while your kid watches.
Ask "where is it?" and let them lift cups until they find it, with a cheer for a first try.
For a kid of 2 and up, hide two toys and see if they remember which cup is already empty.

activities.title: Pocket Kiss
activities.blurb: Good for a parent flat on the sofa, a kid of 2 and up who climbs on, and the last five minutes before bed.
steps: Kiss one of your kid's palms and help them close both hands into fists to keep the kiss in.
Sing one line of any song together, then ask "which hand has the kiss?"
Open the fist they pick, kiss the other palm, and make the wait a little longer each time.

activities.title: New Hiding Spot
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sitting on the floor, two cushions, and a kid who always looks in the same place.
steps: Hide a toy under the left cushion while your kid watches, and let them find it twice.
Now slide it under the right cushion, slowly and in full view, and ask "where now?"
Cheer when they skip the old spot, then let them hide it and you look under the wrong cushion first.

activities.title: Goodnight Room
activities.blurb: Good for the last minute before lights out, a parent already lying down, and a kid of 2 and up who can point.
steps: Say goodnight to three things in the room together, like the lamp, the chair and teddy, pointing at each.
Switch the light off and ask "where is the lamp?" so your kid points to it in the dark.
Light back on to check, then ask for the other two, and let a kid of 2 and up pick the three things.

activities.title: Two in the Picture
activities.blurb: Good for a kid on your lap, a busy picture book, and a parent who would rather not read the words.
steps: Before you turn to a busy page, name two things to find on it, like "a dog and a red hat".
Open the page and let your kid hunt for both while you keep your finger still.
If they find one and stop, ask "and the other one?" instead of pointing.

activities.title: Pat Pat Copy
activities.blurb: Good for a kid leaning on your legs, a quiet room, and a parent whose hands still work.
steps: Pat a short pattern on your knee, like pat pat, and wait for your kid to pat it back on your arm.
Keep it to two pats for a young one, and add a third pat or a clap for a kid of 2 and up.
Swap, so they invent the pattern and you copy it, slipping up now and then so they fix you.

activities.title: Your Name Story
activities.blurb: Good for lying down in the dark with a kid of 2 and up who wants one more story and knows their name.
steps: Start a story with your kid as the hero, like "one day Mia found a tiny door in the garden".
Stop at the exciting bit and ask "what did Mia do?", then use whatever they say.
Keep taking turns, and when they run out, tell the whole story back with every bit they added.

activities.title: Today in Order
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sunk into the sofa and a kid of 2 and up who had a day worth telling.
steps: Say "first we woke up, then we had breakfast" and stop with a big "and then?"
Let your kid name what came next, and add one true detail before handing the next "and then?" back.
Skip something big on purpose, like lunch, and let them catch you.

activities.title: Mystery Hands
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sitting still with a few toys in reach, and a kid of 2 and up who can keep their eyes shut.
steps: Hide a toy inside your cupped hands, and your kid shuts their eyes and pokes one finger in to feel it.
Let them guess what it is before they open their eyes, then open your hands to check.
Swap, so they hide something in their hands and you feel it slowly and guess.

activities.title: Lumpy Blanket
activities.blurb: Good for a parent lying on the sofa, a blanket, and a kid of 2 and up who cannot keep a giggle in yet.
steps: Your kid hides under a blanket beside you and tries to stay still and quiet.
Hunt out loud in silly wrong places, like "in the cup, no, behind the lamp, no", while they hold still.
Find the lump with a gasp, then it is your turn to be the lump while they hunt.

activities.title: Hand on the Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a kitchen floor, a cup over a toy, and a kid of 2 and up who grabs first and asks later.
steps: Put a toy under an upside down cup and rest your kid's hand flat on top.
Say "wait, wait, wait" and then "go", and they lift the cup only on "go".
Stretch the wait a little each time, then let them hold the cup while you wait for their "go".

activities.title: Three Two One Hug
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can only open their arms, and a kid of 2 and up who runs in before you are ready.
steps: Open your arms wide and count down slowly, "three, two, one", while your kid waits a step away.
Say "hug" and they come in for the squeeze, then back up to their spot for another round.
Count slower, or pause before "one", and for a kid of 2 and up let them count you down.

activities.title: Piggy Pause
activities.blurb: Good for a kid on your lap with bare feet, and a parent who knows one toe rhyme.
steps: Say "this little piggy" on each toe, slower with every piggy.
Stop dead before the last piggy and hold your finger in the air until your kid looks up at you.
Finish with the wee wee wee wiggle, and next round make the hush a breath longer.

activities.title: Finger Candle
activities.blurb: Good for a bedtime wind down, a parent on the pillow, and a kid of 2 and up with one speed of blowing.
steps: Hold up one finger as a candle and ask your kid to blow it out.
A quick puff makes the flame flicker and stand straight again, and only a long slow blow folds it down.
Light more fingers, one at a time, and go slow enough that each candle takes one whole breath.

activities.title: Still Stone
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up lying beside you who has one wriggle left, and a parent with one hand free.
steps: Your kid lies still as a stone while your hand becomes a mouse that creeps towards them.
Any wriggle or giggle sends the mouse scurrying back to the start, and holding still brings it closer.
When the mouse reaches them it curls up to sleep on their tummy, then swap and you be the stone.

activities.title: Knee Bridge
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor with knees up, a ball, and a kid of 2 and up who likes a drawbridge.
steps: Lie with your knees bent up so they make a bridge, and your kid rolls the ball under it.
Drop your knees flat and the bridge is shut, so they hold the ball and wait.
Lift them again with a creak and say "open", stretching the shut time a little each go.

activities.title: Touch the Bear
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who wants to lie still with eyes shut, and a kid of 2 and up whose first idea is to shout.
steps: Be a bear asleep on the sofa and tell your kid that shouting only makes a bear snore louder.
Snore louder at every shout, and wake up with a happy growl only when a hand touches your paw.
Swap, so they sleep and you try a shout before you remember to touch.

activities.title: Rug Tightrope
activities.blurb: Good for a rug edge or a line in the floorboards, a parent on the sofa, and a kid of 2 and up.
steps: Point out the edge of the rug as a tightrope that leads to you on the sofa.
Your kid walks it one slow step at a time, arms out, while you narrate every step in a hush.
A foot off the rope means back to the start, and a kid who reaches you gets a sofa hug.

activities.title: Shy Sock
activities.blurb: Good for a parent lying down with a sock on one hand, and a kid of 2 and up with no quiet voice yet.
steps: Put a sock on your hand as a shy puppet that only comes out of your sleeve for whispers.
When your kid whispers to it, the sock creeps out and whispers back, and at any loud word it dives in.
Let the sock ask them whispered questions, like what they ate today, and give it a silly name.

activities.title: Whisper Chat
activities.blurb: Good for a sleeping sibling in the next room and a kid of 2 and up who has just discovered whispering.
steps: Lay a toy down to sleep between you and agree that only whispers are allowed while it sleeps.
Whisper a question, like "what did you eat?", and your kid whispers the answer back.
If anyone talks out loud the toy sits up cross, and you both whisper it back to sleep.

activities.title: Toy Bedtime
activities.blurb: Good for the end of the day, a parent on the bed, and a kid who has toys to put to sleep too.
steps: Gather four toys on the bed and whisper that it is their bedtime too.
Your kid tucks one toy under the cloth at a time, with a whispered "night night" and a kiss.
Ask "who is still awake?" before each tuck, and let them check under the cloth if they forget.

activities.title: Whisper Tent
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor with knees up, a blanket, and a kid of 2 and up who likes rules.
steps: Drape a blanket over your bent knees to make a tent, with one rule: inside the tent, only whispers.
Outside the tent everyone talks normally, so your kid crawls in whispering and pops out loud.
Ask the same question in both places and enjoy them switching their voice each time they cross.

activities.title: Tummy Drum
activities.blurb: Good for a parent flat on their back, a kid of 2 and up who likes to pat, and no sleeping sibling nearby.
steps: Lie back and your tummy is the drum, with your kid as the drummer.
Call "mouse" for tiny soft pats and "elephant" for big slow ones, switching without warning.
Call "stop" and their hands fly up, then swap and let them call the animals while you drum your tummy.

activities.title: Hum and Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can hum but not sing, and a kid of 2 and up who sways to anything.
steps: Hum any tune and sway together while your kid sits on your lap or dances beside you.
Stop humming without warning and freeze, and they freeze too until the hum starts again.
Make the silences longer and the hums shorter, then let them hum and catch you still moving.

activities.title: Magic Word Song
activities.blurb: Good for a song your kid of 2 and up knows by heart, and a parent who can sing it lying down.
steps: Pick a song they know and choose one magic word in it, like "star" in Twinkle Twinkle.
Sing it together, and every time the magic word comes you both clap your hands over your mouths.
Once they catch every one, swap to a new word, and let a kid of 2 and up choose it.

activities.title: Rock the Baby
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up with a doll or teddy to cuddle, a parent who can sing slowly, and a long evening.
steps: Your kid rocks their toy to sleep in their arms while you sing a lullaby slowly.
Sing faster and the rocking gets faster, sing slower and it slows right down to match.
Finish in a whisper so slow the toy falls asleep, then they sing and you rock.

activities.title: Name That Hum
activities.blurb: Good for a parent with eyes shut on the pillow and a kid of 2 and up who knows three songs.
steps: Hum a song your kid knows well without any words.
They guess which song it is and sing the words while you keep humming along.
Swap, so they hum and you guess, taking a long time to get it so they hum it again.

activities.title: Animal Swap
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can only manage a moo, a kid who knows a cow from a duck, and no props at all.
steps: Name an animal and your kid makes its sound, starting with the easy ones like cow and duck.
After five, swap jobs: they name the animal and you make the sound, as badly as you like.
Swap back whenever one of you says "switch", and see how fast you can both change jobs.

activities.title: No Repeat Farm
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can manage Old MacDonald from the sofa and a kid of 2 and up who knows six animals.
steps: Sing Old MacDonald and let your kid choose the animal for each verse.
The one rule is no animal twice, so when they say "cow" again, sing "we had the cow" and wait.
Count the animals on your fingers at the end, and next time you choose and they catch your repeats.

activities.title: Turtle Rabbit Knee
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sitting still with a kid at their knee, and a kid of 2 and up who only has a fast speed.
steps: Your kid's hand walks up your leg from your ankle to your knee as an animal.
Call "turtle" for a hand that creeps so slowly it barely moves, and "rabbit" for one that hops up fast.
Switch animals halfway up the leg, then let them call the animals for your hand.

activities.title: Baby Cup Mummy Cup
activities.blurb: Good for a big cup, a small cup, a parent on the kitchen floor, and a kid of 2 and up who loves nonsense.
steps: Hold up a big cup and a small cup and agree the big one is called "baby" and the small one "mummy".
Hold up one cup at a time and your kid says its silly name, laughing when the big cup is the baby.
Go faster, and when they slip up, hold the cups still and let them have another go.

activities.title: Nod or Shake
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who cannot even sit up and a kid of 2 and up who can nod and shake their head.
steps: Ask silly questions, like "is a cat a bird?", and your kid answers only with a nod or a shake.
No words allowed, so when a "no" slips out, you both shake your heads at it and carry on.
For a kid near 3, swap the rule so a nod means no and a shake means yes, and ask "are you a monkey?"

activities.title: Nose Knees Toes
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the sofa who can lift a hand, and a toddler of 2 and up who knows where their nose is.
steps: Ask "where is your nose?" and touch yours, and your kid touches theirs, then knees, toes, ears.
Once they are quick, say "touch your toes" while you touch your nose, and they follow the words.
Say the parts faster, and for a kid of 2 and up give two at once, like "ears, then tummy".

activities.title: Teddy's Dinner
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sitting on the rug with a teddy, a spoon and a cup, and a kid who likes to feed.
steps: Sit teddy up and ask your kid to feed him pretend porridge from an empty cup with a spoon.
Make teddy talk, asking for "more", then "a drink please", then "no thank you, I am full".
Your kid works out what teddy wants each time, then they do teddy's voice and you feed him.

activities.title: Doctor Kid
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who needs to lie down anyway and a kid who wants to make everything better.
steps: Lie down as the patient and tell the doctor two things that hurt, like "my knee and my elbow".
Your kid checks both spots, wraps one in a cloth or kisses it better, and you say exactly how it feels.
Groan about a new spot, add a toy that is also poorly, then swap and let them be the patient.

activities.title: Face Copy
activities.blurb: Good for a kid sitting on your knees nose to nose, and a parent who can still pull a face.
steps: Make a big face, name it, like "surprised", and hold it until your kid copies it.
Try happy, sleepy, cross and silly, naming each one and holding it still.
Swap, so they pull a face, you copy it, and you both guess what feeling it is.

activities.title: Sleepy Mirror
activities.blurb: Good for the last stretch before sleep, a parent lying down, and a kid of 2 and up who copies everything.
steps: Lie side by side and do everything in slow motion, so a yawn takes a whole breath to finish.
Your kid copies each slow move, a stretch, a roll, a rub of the eyes, at your snail speed.
Let them lead a slow move or two, then end with the slowest eyes closed of all.

activities.title: Sock Phone
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the sofa with one spare sock and a kid who already talks to their teddies.
steps: Hold a sock to your ear as a phone and have a chat with grandma on it.
Now the same sock is a snake slithering up your arm, then a hat, then a glove puppet.
Hand it over and ask "what is it now?", then play along with whatever they decide.

activities.title: Little Seed
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up curled on the rug beside you, a parent who can wiggle fingers, and a slow evening.
steps: Your kid curls up small as a seed on the rug while your fingers sprinkle rain on them.
Count slowly to five and the seed grows a little on each number, reaching the sky on "five".
Call "wind" and the flower sways, "night" and it curls back into a seed, ready to grow again.

activities.title: Find the Twin
activities.blurb: Good for a pile of mixed socks, a parent on the floor, and a toddler of 2 and up who can match.
steps: Spread out three mixed pairs of socks and hold one sock up.
Your kid hunts for its twin while you give one hint at a time, like "look for stripes".
For a kid of 2 and up, give them a good look at your sock, then hide it behind your back while they hunt.

activities.title: Fish or Shark
activities.blurb: Good for a blanket, a parent on the sofa above the sea, and a kid of 2 and up who loves to pop out.
steps: Your kid hides under a blanket on the floor as a fish in the sea.
Call "fish" and they pop out to say hello, but on "shark" they stay hidden and still.
Mix the two words up, add a long silence before each one, then swap so you hide under the blanket.

activities.title: Shadow Zoo
activities.blurb: Good for a dark room, a phone torch, a parent on the bed, and a kid near 3 who likes guessing.
steps: Prop the phone torch so it shines on the wall and put your hand in the beam.
Make a snapping crocodile or a flapping bird with your hand and let your kid guess what it is.
Let them feed the shadow animal with their own shadow hand, then they make one and you guess.

activities.title: Light It Up
activities.blurb: Good for a dim room, a parent who can talk but not get up, and a kid who likes naming things.
steps: Lie back with the phone torch and light up one thing in the room, then your kid names it.
Swap, so they name a thing and you swing the beam onto it, landing on the wrong thing now and then.
When you miss, wait for their "no, the door" before you slide the light across.

activities.title: Ceiling Star
activities.blurb: Good for a dark bedroom, a parent on their back with a phone torch, and a kid lying beside them.
steps: Lie side by side, shine the torch at the ceiling, and glide the spot slowly across it.
Your kid follows the star with their eyes, and when it stops, they point at it.
Switch the torch off, ask "where was it?", and let them point before you switch it back on to check.

activities.title: What Can You Hear
activities.blurb: Good for a parent with eyes shut, a kid who will lie still for a minute, and a house that hums.
steps: Lie still together, close your eyes, and whisper "what can you hear?"
Whatever your kid points at or says, name it with them, like "the fridge" or "a car outside".
Take turns finding one new sound each, and see how long you can both stay quiet enough to hear.

activities.title: Knee Door
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on their back with knees up, and a kid who likes knocking on things.
steps: Lie with your knees up together so they make a closed door, and your kid knocks on it.
Ask "who is there?" and the door opens only after they answer, as themselves or as an animal.
Shut the door with a creak after each visit, and let a kid of 2 and up be the door for your knock.

activities.title: Beep Nose
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who is a machine lying down, and a kid of 2 and up who presses every button they find.
steps: Your nose is a button that beeps, your ear plays a song, and your chin snores.
Your kid presses a button and you do exactly that thing, every time, no matter how often they press.
Add a fourth button on your cheek, then ask "which button snores?" and see if they remember.

activities.title: Give and Take
activities.blurb: Good for the youngest toddlers who have just learnt to hand things over, and a parent in a chair.
steps: Hold a toy out and say "for you", then hold your hand open and wait until your kid gives it back.
Say "thank you" every time and hold the toy a beat longer before you offer it again.
Wait for them to reach or say "more" before each hand over, so they ask and you answer.

activities.title: Which Side
activities.blurb: Good for a parent behind a cushion on the sofa, one toy, and a young toddler who loves a surprise.
steps: Hold a cushion up in front of your face and pop a toy up over the left edge with a "boo".
Pop it up on the right, then left again, so your kid starts to look where it will come next.
Pause before a pop, and when they are looking at the right side, let the toy give them a kiss.

activities.title: Find My Foot
activities.blurb: Good for a parent happy to lie under a blanket, and a kid who can tell a foot from a hand.
steps: Lie under a blanket from head to toe and say "find my foot".
Your kid pulls the blanket off only that part, and you wiggle it, then cover up and name another.
For a kid of 2 and up, ask for two parts at once, like "my hand and then my nose".

activities.title: Peekaboo Faces
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sitting with a tea towel, and a young toddler who still thinks peekaboo is magic.
steps: Hold a cloth in front of your face and drop it to show a huge happy face, saying "happy".
Lift it, and drop it again with a sad face, a sleepy face, a surprised face, naming each one.
Hold the cloth up a little longer each time, then ask "what face is coming?" before you drop it.

activities.title: In On Under
activities.blurb: Good for a cup and a rolled sock on the floor, a parent sitting beside them, and a young toddler.
steps: Put a cup on the floor, hand your kid a rolled sock, and say "put it in the cup".
Next ask for the sock on the cup, under the cup, and behind the cup, one place at a time.
Let them say a place for you and do it, and for a kid of 2 and up, give two places in a row.

activities.title: Cloth Riddle
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the sofa with a tea towel over a toy, and a kid near 3 who likes clues.
steps: Hide one of their toys under a cloth while they look away.
Give one clue at a time, like "it has wheels", and they guess before anyone lifts the cloth.
Lift it together to check, then swap and let them hide a toy and give you a clue.

activities.title: Scarf Up Scarf Down
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can lift one arm, a scarf, and a kid of 2 and up who needs to wiggle it out.
steps: Hold a scarf up high and your kid wiggles and dances while it is up.
Drop the scarf into your lap and they freeze like a statue until it goes up again.
Keep the scarf down longer each time, and for a kid near 3 swap it so down means dance and up means freeze.

activities.title: Teddy's Turn
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the rug with cups or blocks, a teddy, and a kid who cannot wait for a turn.
steps: Build a tower in strict turns: you place one, then teddy places one, then your kid.
Your kid moves teddy's paw for his turn and must wait through yours and his before their own.
Ask "whose turn?" before each block, and for a young one drop teddy and take turns just the two of you.

activities.title: Shy Tortoises
activities.blurb: Good for a parent under a blanket with cold feet, and a kid of 2 and up who finds it hard not to look.
steps: Your feet under the blanket are two shy tortoises that only poke out when your kid shuts their eyes.
Eyes shut, the tortoises creep out and wiggle, and the moment they peek, both dive back under.
Count to three with eyes shut so the tortoises come right out, then they open them and catch the pair.

activities.title: Open Shut Them
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up on your lap, a parent who knows one finger rhyme, and a slow wind down.
steps: Sing "open, shut them" with your hands, and your kid copies each open and shut.
Creep your fingers up to your chin and stop right there on "but do not let them in".
Do the creep slower every time, and watch them hold their own fingers at the chin without going in.

activities.title: Fill the Rhyme
activities.blurb: Good for a parent in bed beside their kid, and a kid who knows a rhyme well enough to notice when it stops.
steps: Sing a rhyme your kid knows and go silent right before the last word of a line.
Wait, with your mouth open and eyebrows up, until they say the word, then carry on.
Leave out two words in a row for a kid of 2 and up, and let them stop a line for you.

activities.title: Same or Different
activities.blurb: Good for a parent sunk into the sofa with the sock pile, and a kid of 2 and up who knows the word "same".
steps: Hold up two socks, one in each hand, and ask "same or different?" while your kid looks hard.
Help them answer with the word or a nod, then swap one sock and ask again.
Let them hold up two for you, and get it wrong now and then so they can put you right.

activities.title: Wash Then Dry
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the sofa, a teddy, a tea towel, and a kid who likes a job with two parts.
steps: Tell your kid that teddy is muddy, so first he gets a wash with their hands, then a dry with the cloth.
Say the plan back together, "wash, then dry", before they start.
If the cloth comes first, ask "what comes first?" instead of fixing it, then they plan the next job.

activities.title: One Finger Wiggle
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up lying beside you, and a parent who can lift one hand and nothing else.
steps: Hold up one hand and wiggle only your thumb, with every other finger as still as a stone.
Touch one of your kid's fingers and ask them to wiggle just that one while the rest stay still.
Pick a new finger each time, then wiggle one of yours and let them find the same finger on their hand.

activities.title: You Say Three
activities.blurb: Good for a kid on your lap who is starting to count, and a parent who can manage three bounces.
steps: Bounce your kid on your knee and count "one, two", then stop dead with your hands in the air.
Wait, eyebrows up, until they say "three", then give the biggest bounce of all.
Count claps, toes and taps the same way, and sometimes stop before "two" instead.

activities.title: Please Puppet
activities.blurb: Good for a parent in a chair with a sock on one hand, and a kid of 2 and up who grabs first and never asks.
steps: Put a sock on your hand as a puppet who holds a toy in its mouth and only lets go for the word "please".
When hands grab, the puppet shakes its head and holds on, and when the word comes, it drops the toy at once.
Let the puppet ask for the toy back with a "please" of its own, then give your kid the sock.

activities.title: Pass the Kiss
activities.blurb: Good for the sofa at the end of the day, a teddy, and a kid who likes everyone to have a turn.
steps: Kiss your own palm, press it to your kid's cheek, and say "pass it on".
They kiss their palm and pass the kiss to teddy, and teddy passes it back to you.
Add a second toy to the chain, and ask "who is next?" before each pass.

activities.title: Cushion Shuffle
activities.blurb: Good for a sofa full of cushions and a kid who already loves peekaboo, with the swap from about 2.
steps: Lay three cushions on the floor and tuck a toy under one while your kid watches.
Ask "where is it?" and let them lift cushions until they find it.
Hide it again, slide two cushions past each other slowly in front of them, and ask once more.

activities.title: Two Sock Piles
activities.blurb: Good for the laundry pile, a sitting parent, and a kid of 2 and up who likes putting things in places.
steps: Tip a heap of clean socks on the floor and start two piles, dark socks here and light socks there.
Pass one sock at a time and let them choose the pile, with a hint only when they stall.
Once the heap is gone, mix it up and start again, but now big socks here and little socks there.

activities.title: Two in One Breath
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting parent, a room full of toys, and a kid of 2 and up who loves being sent on a mission.
steps: Sit down and ask for two things in one breath, like "bring me the cup and the duck".
Stay where you are and cheer each thing as it arrives, even if only one makes it.
When two is easy, ask for three, and let them send you for two.

activities.title: Slow Motion Me
activities.blurb: Good for five minutes before the bath, a parent on their feet, and a kid of 2 and up who copies everything.
steps: Face your kid and lift one arm as slowly as you can, like you are moving through honey.
Keep going with slow moves, a slow turn, a slow sit, and let them copy at your speed.
If they speed up, go even slower, and whisper "sloooow" together.

activities.title: Cat Toes, Bear Feet
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who stomps anyway, a parent who can stroll, and a room with a soft floor.
steps: Say "cat" and both of you tiptoe around the room without a sound.
Say "bear" and switch to big slow stomps with a growl.
Swap the word more and more often, then let them be the one who calls it.

activities.title: Teddy's Cafe
activities.blurb: Good for a parent in a chair, a cup and a spoon, and a kid of 2 and up who likes being in charge.
steps: Sit down as the customer and order two things from your kid, the waiter, like "tea and a banana".
They walk off to the kitchen corner, pretend to make it, and carry it back to you.
Taste it, ask "and the banana?" if they forgot, then swap and take their order.

activities.title: Who Ran Away
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor and a kid of 2 and up, with any three toys within reach.
steps: Line up three toys and name each one together.
Your kid covers their eyes while you tuck one toy behind your back, then ask "who ran away?".
When they guess right, the toy comes back with a hello, and after a few goes they hide and you guess.

activities.title: Tower on Three
activities.blurb: Good for a stacking kid of 2 and up who really just wants to knock, and a parent sitting on the rug.
steps: Build a tower of cups or blocks while your kid waits with their hands in their lap.
Count "one, two" very slowly, with a long look at each other before "three".
On "three" they smash it down, then you build again, and this time they count.

activities.title: Speedy Sleepy Song
activities.blurb: Good for any action song you both know, a sitting parent, and a kid of 2 and up who needs to wind down.
steps: Sing an action song you both know at normal speed, with the actions.
Sing it again faster, then faster still, until the actions are a blur.
Then sing it as slowly as a yawn, stretching every action out, and end in a whisper.

activities.title: Wait, Wait, Go
activities.blurb: Good for a ball, a kid of 2 and up, two people on the floor with legs apart, and a parent not getting up.
steps: Sit facing each other with your legs apart and the ball in your kid's hands.
Say "wait, wait" slowly while they hold it, then "go", and they roll it to you.
Stretch the wait a little longer each time, then let them say the words to you.

activities.title: Warm and Cold
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up, one favourite toy, and a parent who can direct the search from the sofa.
steps: Send your kid to the door, hide the toy somewhere in the room, and call them back.
Say "warm" in a cosy voice as they get closer and "cold" with a shiver as they drift away.
When they find it, they hide it for you and try the warm and cold words themselves.

activities.title: Two Homes
activities.blurb: Good for the end of the day, a kid of 2 and up, a floor full of toys, and a parent who would like them gone.
steps: Pick two homes, like a shelf for the blocks and the sofa for the soft toys, and show each one once.
Hand your kid things one at a time and ask "where does it live?" while you stay put.
Cheer every right home, and when a block lands on the sofa, ask the question again.

activities.title: Cup Drum Turns
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who bangs on everything, two cups, and a parent who can sit through the noise.
steps: Turn two cups upside down, one each, and say "my turn" before you tap a short beat.
Say "your turn" and keep your hands still while your kid taps back.
Make your beats a little longer each time, and keep your hands flat on the floor until they say "your turn".

activities.title: Sock Bowling
activities.blurb: Good for a rolled sock, one cup, a long rug, and a parent who stays on the cushion the whole time.
steps: Stand a cup at the far end of the rug and sit your kid beside you with a rolled sock.
The rule is rolling, not throwing, so roll the first one together with your hand over theirs.
After each knock they stand the cup up and come back, and if they forget a step you ask "what next?".

activities.title: Behind My Back
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up, two small toys, and a parent who can play it from any chair.
steps: Sit with two toys hidden behind your back, show your kid one of them, name it, and tuck it back out of sight.
Bring out the other toy and ask "is this it?", then look amazed when they shake their head.
Bring out the right one with a cheer, then let them hide two behind their back and trick you.

activities.title: Simon Says Two
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can stand still, and a kid of 2 and up who knows their nose from their toes.
steps: Say "Simon says touch your nose, then clap" and wait while they do both in order.
Keep to two actions a go, and when they manage both, say the two back to them.
Swap, and do exactly what they say, even if it is "touch your nose, then touch your nose".

activities.title: Turtle Rabbit Lines
activities.blurb: Good for a table, one crayon and some paper, and a kid of 2 and up who can hold a crayon.
steps: Draw a slow turtle line across the page, saying "tuuurtle", and let your kid draw one under it.
Now draw a fast rabbit line with a quick "rabbit" and let them race one too.
Call "turtle" or "rabbit" before each new line, and switch more and more often.

activities.title: Mirror Twins
activities.blurb: Good for any big mirror, a parent sitting behind their kid, and a kid who loves their own face.
steps: Sit behind your kid facing a mirror and pull a slow face, like a big surprised mouth.
Watch them copy it in the mirror, and make the next face only after they have matched yours.
Say "your turn" and copy every face they make, as exactly as you can.

activities.title: Follow My Finger
activities.blurb: Good for a sitting parent, a kid of any age from 1, and a room you do not need to tidy first.
steps: Hold up one finger in front of your kid and move it slowly from side to side while they watch.
Draw slow loops in the air and land on something in the room, saying its name when their eyes get there.
Then point at a spot on the floor and let their feet follow the finger over to it.

activities.title: Ring Ring
activities.blurb: Good for a parent slumped on the sofa, a block or a shoe for a phone, and a kid who loves to chat.
steps: Hold a block to your ear, say "ring ring", and hand your kid a block of their own to answer.
Ask one question, then go quiet and hold the phone to your ear until they say something back.
Say "bye bye" and hang up, then wait for them to ring you.

activities.title: One More, Then Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who loves to thump the sofa, and a parent who wants the thumping to end.
steps: Thump a sofa cushion together as fast as you both can.
Say "one more, then stop", and after one last thump everyone puts their hands in their lap.
Count a slow three in a whisper, then thump again.

activities.title: Spoon Bell
activities.blurb: Good for the high chair, a kid of 2 and up, one bite of something they love, and a spoon and a cup.
