steps: Put one favourite bite under an upturned cup on the tray and show your kid the spoon.
Say "wait for the bell", pause, then tap the spoon on the table twice.
On the tap they lift the cup and eat, and the next wait is a bit longer.

activities.title: Cloth Present
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor with a towel, and a kid of 2 and up who finds not peeking very hard.
steps: Sit your kid facing the sofa, say "no peeking", and wrap a toy in a towel behind them, rustling a lot.
Count to ten out loud, then say "open", and they turn round and unwrap it.
Swap, so they wrap something for you while you cover your eyes and count.

activities.title: Look Where I Look
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who has only just turned 1, a parent sitting on the floor, and a room with things to look at.
steps: Sit by your kid and turn your head to look hard at one thing across the room, saying its name.
When their eyes land on it too, say the name again and wait for them to toddle to it or point.
Then follow their gaze instead and name whatever they are looking at, for as long as they look.

activities.title: Window Spotter
activities.blurb: Good for a rainy afternoon, a window with a street, and a parent who can sit with a kid on their knee.
steps: Sit at the window with your kid on your knee and choose one thing to wait for, like a red car or a dog.
Watch quietly together, and when it comes, say "there" and name it at the same time.
Pick the next thing to wait for together, and let them say "there" first.

activities.title: Page Patrol
activities.blurb: Good for a picture book you both know by heart, and a parent happy to let their kid do the pointing.
steps: Pick one thing that is on every page of the book, like the cat or the moon, and show it on the first page.
On every page after that, read the words, then wait until your kid finds it and points.
Say its name together each time, and when the book ends, start again with a new thing to find.

activities.title: What Comes Next
activities.blurb: Good for bedtime, a story your kid of 2 and up knows by heart, and a parent on their hundredth read.
steps: Read a favourite story and stop just before you turn each page.
Ask "what comes next?" and wait for your kid to tell you, with words or by pointing.
Turn the page, see if they were right, and cheer either way.

activities.title: Loud and Soft
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who sings at one volume, which is loud, and a parent who can manage a quiet one.
steps: Sing a song together, and when you raise your hand high you both sing loud.
Lower your hand to your knee and both of you drop to a whisper, still singing.
Hand over the job, so your kid's hand decides how loud you sing.

activities.title: Cup Hat
activities.blurb: Good for one cup, a parent who can sit still, and a kid who is just discovering pretend.
steps: Put a cup on your head, say "hat", and let your kid try it on.
Drink from it as a giant, drive it along the floor as a car, sail it as a boat, and name each new thing.
Hand it over and ask "what is it now?", then play along with whatever they say.

activities.title: What Next Tower
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who wants to do it all by themselves, and a parent who is good at sitting on their hands.
steps: Tip out the blocks or cups, say "let's build a tall one", then keep your hands in your lap.
When they stop, ask "what next?" instead of adding a block yourself.
If a piece will not fit, point at where it might go and let them try.

activities.title: Something Soft
activities.blurb: Good for a parent in a chair, a kid of 2 and up, and a room with a bit of everything in it.
steps: Ask your kid to bring you something soft, and squeeze whatever comes to check.
Next ask for something red, then something round, then something that makes a noise.
Make a little pile of everything they brought and name each one as they carry it back.

activities.title: Still Water
activities.blurb: Good for a bath that is already happening, a splashy kid of 2 and up, and a parent kneeling at the side.
steps: Splash the water together with your hands for a few seconds.
Say "still water" and both of you hold your hands up and watch the ripples go flat.
When the water is flat as glass, say "splash" and go again.

activities.title: Spotlight Fetch
activities.blurb: Good for a dim evening room, a phone torch, and a kid of 2 and up who wants to toddle about before bed.
steps: Dim the room, shine the phone torch on one toy on the floor, and name it.
They may step into the light only once it stops moving, so wobble it about a bit before you let it settle.
Move the spotlight to the next toy only after the last one is in your lap.

activities.title: Robot Parent
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who is told what to do all day, and a parent happy to take orders for once.
steps: Stand stiff like a robot and say in a flat voice "what should the robot do?".
Do exactly what your kid says, one order at a time, whether it is sit, clap or touch the door.
If the order is impossible, say "robot cannot" and wait for a new one.

activities.title: Show and Name
activities.blurb: Good for a parent on the floor and a kid who has only just turned 1 and keeps handing you things.
steps: Sit on the floor and take whatever your kid hands you, naming it and one thing about it.
Hand it back and wait, with your hands open, until they bring the next thing.
If they look up at you while holding something, say what you think they like about it.

activities.title: Upside Down Sort
activities.blurb: Good for a big cup, a little cup, a pile of socks, and a kid of 2 and up who likes a joke.
steps: Put big socks in the big cup and little socks in the little cup, with your kid helping.
Then call "upside down", and now big socks squash into the little cup and little ones go in the big cup.
Hand over socks one at a time and laugh together every time a big one tries to sneak into the big cup.

activities.title: Sound Effects Story
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who can make up a story about a cow, a dog and a duck, and a kid who does the noises.
steps: Tell a tiny story with a cow, a dog and a duck in it, and agree your kid makes every animal noise.
Each time an animal turns up, pause and wait for the noise before the story goes on.
Bring back the same three animals in a muddle so they have to pick the right noise each time.

activities.title: You Be Me
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who knows the bedtime drill, and a parent happy to be tucked in for once.
steps: Say "you be the grown up, I am the baby" and curl up on the sofa.
Ask "is it bedtime?" in a tiny voice and let them tuck a blanket round you and boss you about.
Do what the grown up says, yawn a lot, and ask for a story.

activities.title: Roll to Teddy
activities.blurb: Good for a ball, a soft toy sat up on the rug, and a parent who can sit with their legs apart.
steps: Sit on the floor with a toy propped up beside you and the ball with your kid.
Call the toy's name or "me", and they roll the ball to whoever you named before you roll it back.
Switch the name more often as they get the hang of it, then let them call for you.

activities.title: Page Turner
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who turns the page before you have finished, and a parent who wants to read the words.
steps: Read a book with your kid holding the corner of the page.
They turn only when you say "turn", so read the page slowly, then look at them and say it.
Swap, so you hold the corner and wait for them to say "turn".

activities.title: Peek and Pick
activities.blurb: Good for a handful of odd socks, a cloth, and a kid of 2 and up who likes a little puzzle.
steps: Lay out one sock from each of three pairs, and keep the three twins in your lap.
Show one twin for a slow count of three, hide it under a cloth, and ask "which one is it?".
They pick from the three on the floor, then lift the cloth together to check.

activities.title: Secret Keeper
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who cannot keep a secret yet, and a parent who searches from the sofa.
steps: Cover your eyes while your kid hides a toy somewhere in the room.
Search from your seat, out loud, in all the wrong places, and their job is to not point.
After three wrong guesses, say "one clue please" and let them give you one.

activities.title: Copy Tower
activities.blurb: Good for a few blocks or cups, a tea towel, and a kid of 2 and up who likes to build.
steps: Build a tiny tower of two or three blocks and let your kid look at it for a slow count of three.
Drop a cloth over it and ask them to build the same one beside it, asking "what next?" if they stall.
Lift the cloth, compare the two together, then let them build one for you to copy.

activities.title: Teddy Queue
activities.blurb: Good for three soft toys in a row, one cup, and a kid who wants everyone to have a turn.
steps: Sit three toys in a row and give your kid a cup, so each toy gets a sip in turn, left to right.
Then start a round of pats on the head, asking "who is next?" and waiting for them to pick the right toy.
Change the order of the toys and go round again, with the cup and then the pats.

activities.title: Red Light Whisper
activities.blurb: Good for a parent in the passenger seat, a kid of 2 and up in the car seat, and a drive with red lights.
steps: When the car stops at a red light, say "red light" and drop to a whisper together.
When it moves off, say "green" and go back to normal voices.
Let your kid be the one who spots the red light and starts the whispering.

activities.title: Pass on the Beat
activities.blurb: Good for a ball or a rolled sock, two people on the floor, and a parent who can sing one slow song.
steps: Sit facing your kid, hold the ball, and sing a slow song you both know.
At the end of every line say "pass" and hand the ball over, and they hand it back at the end of the next line.
Sing slower so the wait gets longer, then faster so the passes come quick, and let them say the "pass".

activities.title: Three Splashes
activities.blurb: Good for a bath that is already happening, a splashy kid of 2 and up, and a parent kneeling close by.
steps: Agree on three splashes, count them out loud together, and stop with both hands held high after the third.
Hold still for a slow breath, then agree a new number, like two or five, and go again.
Let your kid pick the number and lead the count, and a splash after the last number means you both start over.

activities.title: Odd Sock Out
activities.blurb: Good for the laundry pile, a parent sitting in it, and a kid of 2 and up who spots the stranger.
steps: Lay out three socks, two from one pair and one stranger, and ask "which one is different?"
When they point to the stranger, swap it for a new one and lay the three out again.
Make it harder with socks that are nearly the same, then let them set out three for you.

activities.title: Whisper Feet
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who stomps, and a parent who can walk a slow lap of the room.
steps: Walk round the room together, and the rule is that your voice sets their feet.
When you whisper, their feet go on tiptoe, and when you talk in a big voice they stomp.
Switch your voice without warning, then swap so their voice drives your feet.

activities.title: Line Them Up
activities.blurb: Good for three toys, a parent on the floor, and a kid of 2 and up who likes things in a row.
steps: Name two toys in order, like "bear, then car", and your kid lines them up left to right as you said.
Check the line together, then name three in a row for the next line.
Swap, so they call the order and you line them up, getting one wrong for them to fix.

activities.title: Red Means Clap
activities.blurb: Good for a room with some red in it, a parent who can point, and a kid of 2 and up who knows their colours.
steps: Point at things round the room one at a time, and your kid claps only when the thing is red.
Point at a lot of red things in a row, then at something blue, and see if the hands stay still.
Swap the colour to blue, then let your kid point while you clap.

activities.title: Tell Teddy
activities.blurb: Good for a teddy across the room, a parent in a chair, and a kid of 2 and up who loves a secret.
steps: Sit teddy on the far side of the room and whisper a short message to your kid, like "teddy, dinner time".
They walk over and tell teddy the message, and you answer in teddy's voice if it arrived whole.
Make the message one word longer each time, then teddy sends one back to you.

activities.title: Ready Sock
activities.blurb: Good for a table or the floor, one rolled sock, and a parent who waits for their kid's word for once.
steps: Hold a rolled sock ready to slide across to your kid, and do not move it until they say "ready".
The moment the word comes, slide it over, and wait again with your hand still until they say it next time.
Swap roles, so they hold the sock and slide it only on your "ready", and wait as long as you dare.

activities.title: Backwards Steps
activities.blurb: Good for a cleared bit of floor, two hands to hold, and a kid of 2 and up who has only walked forwards.
steps: Hold both of your kid's hands and walk them slowly backwards towards the sofa, one step at a time.
Count each step out loud together and stop still whenever you say "freeze".
Turn round and let them walk you backwards, calling the freezes themselves.

activities.title: Does It Roll
activities.blurb: Good for a floor full of toys, a cushion for the rollers, and a kid of 2 and up who likes to test things.
steps: Pick up a toy, ask "does it roll?", and give it a push along the floor to find out.
Rollers go on the cushion and the rest go in a pile, and your kid sorts the next toy after one push.
When the floor is clear, start again with a new question, like "is it soft?", and sort them all over.

activities.title: Build What I Say
activities.blurb: Good for a few cups or blocks in two colours, a parent on the rug, and a kid of 2 and up who listens.
steps: Say a tiny tower out loud, like "red, then blue", and your kid builds it in that order.
Check it together, then say three colours for the next tower.
Swap, so they call the colours and you build, asking "what next?" when they go quiet.

activities.title: Pat the Moo
activities.blurb: Good for three toys in a row, a parent who does the noises, and a kid who can point.
steps: Sit three toys in a row and agree a noise for each, like "moo" for the cow and "beep" for the car.
Make one noise without looking at the toys, and your kid pats the one that makes it.
Shuffle the row, add a fourth toy with a new noise, then they make the noise and you pat.

activities.title: Elbows Only
activities.blurb: Good for a few rolled socks on the floor, and a kid of 2 and up whose hands grab before they think.
steps: Spread a few rolled socks on the floor and ask your kid to pick one up using only their elbows.
Next call "two fingers", then "feet", then "chin and shoulder", and the hands stay out of it each time.
Let them call a body part for you, and drop a sock or two on purpose.

activities.title: Wrong Song
activities.blurb: Good for a song your kid of 2 and up knows every word of, and a parent happy to get it wrong.
steps: Sing a song they know well and swap one word for a silly one, like "twinkle twinkle little sock".
Your kid shouts "no" and sings the right word, then you carry on.
Sing some lines with nothing wrong at all, so they have to listen to every word.

activities.title: Say Then Go
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who runs before they think, and a parent who can watch from a chair.
steps: Your kid points at a place in the room and says it out loud, like "the chair", before their feet move.
Only after the words do they go there, and a run with no words means a walk back to try again.
Make it two places in a row for the older end, and take a turn saying and going yourself.

activities.title: Back Where It Was
activities.blurb: Good for a room with a few toys in their usual places, and a kid of 2 and up who notices.
steps: While your kid watches, move one toy from its spot to somewhere odd, like the car onto the sofa arm.
Count to five together, then ask "where did it live?" and let them carry it back to the exact spot.
Move two toys at once when one is easy, and let them move one for you to put back.

activities.title: Zipped Lips
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a kid of 2 and up who squeals at everything, and a parent with a few silly noises.
steps: Zip your lips together with a pretend zip and walk the hallway side by side in total silence.
Make silly noises along the way, and their lips stay zipped until the far door, where you both shout.
Swap, so they make the noises and you keep your lips zipped.

activities.title: Nose First
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who knows their body parts, and a parent who can cross a room slowly.
steps: Call a body part, like "nose", and both of you cross the room with that part leading the way.
Call a new part for the way back, like "elbow" or "tummy", and change it halfway when they get good.
Let your kid call the parts for you, and lead with whatever they say.

activities.title: Behind You
activities.blurb: Good for a kid near 3 who knows the room, and a parent who only has to ask a question.
steps: Stand your kid facing you with their back to the room and ask "what is behind you?"
They name one thing without turning round, then turn to check and point at it.
Ask for two things next time, and swap so you face away and they test you.

activities.title: Green Means Go
activities.blurb: Good for a long room, a kid of 2 and up who loves to run, and a parent with three laps left in them.
steps: Stand side by side at one end of the room and say "green" so you both run for the far wall.
Call "red" at any moment and both of you stop dead, however far you got.
Take turns calling, and when your kid calls the colours, be a terrible stopper who skids and wobbles.

activities.title: Chase and Freeze
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who needs chasing and a parent who can still manage a slow jog.
steps: Chase your kid round the room with your arms out, slow enough that they stay just ahead.
Shout "freeze" and both of you stop like statues, then count a slow three before the chase goes on.
Let your kid shout it too, and if they say "stop" the chase is over for real.

activities.title: Snail and Rocket
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who only has one speed and a parent who can keep up with the rocket half.
steps: Say "snail" and both of you cross the room as slowly as a snail, with slow arms too.
Say "rocket" and whoosh to the far wall as fast as you can.
Switch the word sooner and sooner, then let your kid be the one who says it.

activities.title: Chair Tunnels
activities.blurb: Good for the kitchen chairs, a kid who loves going under things, and knees that can take a carpet.
steps: Line up two or three chairs in a row to make a tunnel, with a cushion at the end as the finish.
Crawl through first, slowly, so your kid sees the way, then follow them through.
Ask "what next?" instead of pointing when they stop, and after a few runs add a cushion to climb over.

activities.title: Silly Walk Leader
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a kid who copies everything, and a parent who can still waddle.
steps: Walk up the hallway in a silly way, like a wobbly penguin, with your kid behind you copying.
Change the walk every few steps, and at the end turn round and say "your turn".
Copy whatever walk they invent, exactly, even if it is just stamping.

activities.title: Jump, Jump, Freeze
activities.blurb: Good for five minutes before the bath with a kid of 2 and up, when the wiggles need to come out and stop.
steps: Hold hands and jump together while you count "one, two, three", then say "freeze" and hold still.
Count a little higher each round, and keep your feet glued until your kid stops wobbling.
Let them count the jumps, and freeze exactly when they say so, even if that is at two.

activities.title: Dance Till It Stops
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who stops the music, a parent who freezes mid-move, and one loud song.
steps: Put on a song and dance together with your biggest moves, arms and all.
Pause the song mid-beat, and both of you freeze until it plays again.
Let your kid say "stop" and pause it the moment they do, then play it again on their "go".

activities.title: Sock Delivery
activities.blurb: Good for the laundry pile, a kid of 2 and up who insists on carrying things, and a careful walk.
steps: Fill two cups with rolled socks, right to the brim, one for each of you.
Walk them to the sofa without a sock falling out, and if one drops, stop, put it back, and carry on.
Tip them out, add one more sock each, and deliver again.

activities.title: Clap Statues
activities.blurb: Good for a noisy mood, no props at all, and a kid of 2 and up who can hold still for about two seconds.
steps: Both of you wiggle, jump and run about while you hum.
Clap once, and everyone turns into a statue in whatever shape they are in.
Clap twice to melt the statues, and after a few goes your kid does the clapping.

activities.title: Run to the Door
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who knows the names of things, and two things in a row from about two.
steps: Name one thing in the room, like "the door", and race your kid to touch it.
Jog back together, name the next thing, and go again.
From about two, name two in order, "the door, then the sofa", and see if they get both.

activities.title: Terrible Hider
activities.blurb: Good for the first hide and seek, when your kid cannot count yet but loves finding your feet.
steps: Tell your kid to stay on the rug, then hide badly behind a chair, counting to five out loud the whole time.
Call "come and find me" and keep counting from your spot so your voice gives you away.
Swap, counting out loud while they hide, and look in two wrong places before you find them.

activities.title: Airplane Landing
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who wants to be picked up and a parent whose arms have five minutes in them.
steps: Scoop your kid up like a plane, arms out, and fly a slow lap of the room with engine noises.
Say "coming in to land, three, two, one" and set them down gently on the sofa at "one".
Wait for them to say "up" before the next flight, and let them do the countdown when they can.

activities.title: Stair Counter
activities.blurb: Good for the stairs you are climbing anyway with a kid of 2 and up, hand in hand, one step at a time.
steps: Hold your kid's hand and climb the stairs one step at a time, counting each step out loud together.
Say "wait" on one step, stop, and look down at how far you have come before you carry on.
Come back down the same way, step by step, with them doing the counting.

activities.title: Hallway Relay
activities.blurb: Good for a long hallway, a fetcher of 2 and up, and a parent who takes their turn running too.
steps: Put a cup, a sock and a toy at the far end of the hallway and stand at the near end with your kid.
Name one thing, and they run to fetch it and bring it back to you before you name the next.
Then it is your turn to run while they name what to fetch, so take the wrong thing now and then.

activities.title: Clap, New Animal
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who loves animals, a parent with a good frog, and a room with space to stomp.
steps: Stomp round the room as elephants, trunks swinging and trumpeting.
Clap once and call a new animal, like "frog", and both of you change at once.
Clap sooner each time, and when your kid claps, you change into whatever they call.

activities.title: Feet Follow Claps
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who runs at one speed and a parent happy to run on the spot.
steps: Clap slowly and both of you step in time, one step for every clap.
Speed the claps up until you are both running on the spot, then slow right down to a creep.
Give your kid the claps, and move exactly as fast as they clap, even when it is a muddle.

activities.title: Cup Drum Parade
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who marches everywhere anyway and a parent with one cup and a loud voice.
steps: Turn a cup upside down, bang it like a drum, and march round the house with your kid behind you.
Stop the drum without warning and the whole band stops mid-step until it starts again.
Give your kid the drum and march only while it bangs, with a wobble each time it stops.

activities.title: Stop at the Cushion
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who runs into everything, and a parent who can sprint a few short dashes.
steps: Put a cushion in the middle of the floor and stand with your kid at the wall.
Say "go" and both run at the cushion, stopping with your toes touching it and not a step past.
Move the cushion closer to the wall so there is less room to slow down, then let them say go.

activities.title: Big Steps, Tiny Steps
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who likes to count and a parent whose legs can still do a giant stride.
steps: Cross the room in the biggest steps you both can, counting each one out loud.
Come back in tiny mouse steps, heel to toe, counting those too, and marvel at how high the number goes.
Call "big" or "tiny" halfway across so you both change mid-step, counting on from where you were.

activities.title: Roll, Wait, Go
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a ball, and a kid of 2 and up who wants to chase it the second it leaves your hand.
steps: Crouch at one end of the hallway with your kid beside you and roll the ball away down the hall.
Hold hands and watch it roll, and only when it has stopped and you say "go" do you both chase it.
Make the wait after it stops a little longer each time, then let your kid say go.

activities.title: Leg Tunnel
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who crawls through anything and a parent who can stand with their legs apart.
steps: Stand with your legs wide apart and say "tunnel open" so your kid crawls through.
Snap your legs together and say "tunnel closed" so they wait, then open again once they are still.
Take a step forward between each go so the tunnel moves across the room.

activities.title: Cushion Lava
activities.blurb: Good for every cushion in the house, a kid of 2 and up who loves to hop, and a parent who hops too.
steps: Scatter the cushions across the floor and say the floor is lava, so feet stay on cushions.
Hop from cushion to cushion together to reach the sofa, holding hands for the big gaps.
Say "lava rising" and take one cushion away each round, with a "hot, hot, hot" for any toe that slips.

activities.title: Blanket Parachute
activities.blurb: Good for one blanket, a kid who loves the whoosh, and a quiet moment hiding underneath.
steps: Hold a blanket by two corners and let your kid hold the others, or just the edge.
Lift it high together saying "up", let it float down saying "down", three times over.
On the fourth "up" shout "under" and both duck underneath, then sit in the tent and whisper.

activities.title: Cloth River
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who has just learned to jump and a parent who can leap a towel a dozen times.
steps: Lay a scarf or towel flat on the floor as a thin river, and stand on the bank together.
Say "ready" and wait until your kid is still, then "jump" and both leap to the other side.
Open the cloth a bit wider after every jump, and anyone who lands in the river shakes off the water.

activities.title: Whoa, Horse
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who wants a ride and a parent whose knees can take the rug for eight minutes.
steps: Get on all fours on the rug as a horse, and let your kid climb on your back and hold your shoulders.
Walk on when they say "go" and stop dead when they say "whoa", however often they switch.
Swap, so they crawl as the horse while you walk beside them calling go and whoa.

activities.title: Elevator Up
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who knows a few numbers, and arms that can do a few slow lifts.
steps: Hold your kid under the arms, ask "which floor?", and let them pick one, two or three.
Lift them slowly, counting each floor as they rise, and stop with a "ding" at the floor they picked.
Set them down slowly as the doors open, and ask for the next floor.

activities.title: Wake the Bear
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who loves a scare they can see coming, and a parent who lies down between roars.
steps: Lie on the floor as a snoring bear with a rolled sock beside your paw, and send your kid to the sofa.
They tiptoe over to steal the sock, and whenever your snore stutters they must freeze on the spot.
The moment the sock is gone, wake with a roar and chase them back to the sofa, their safe cave.

activities.title: Bridge and Log
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who climbs all over you anyway, and a parent happy to be furniture for a bit.
steps: Make a bridge on your hands and knees and say "bridge", so your kid crawls under your tummy.
Drop flat on the floor and say "log", so they step over your legs instead.
Switch between the two faster and faster, and from about two let them call which one you are.

activities.title: Spot Chase
activities.blurb: Good for a dark evening, the phone torch, and a kid of 2 and up who will chase anything that moves.
steps: Dim the room, shine the phone torch on the floor, and let your kid stamp on the bright spot.
Slide the spot away as they chase it, and when you switch the torch off everyone freezes till it is back.
Hand over the torch and chase the spot yourself, freezing whenever they switch it off.

activities.title: Opposite Day
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who finds wrong answers hilarious, and a parent who can crouch.
steps: Call "up" and both stretch to the ceiling, call "down" and both crouch to the floor, faster and faster.
Then say "opposite day", so now "up" means crouch and "down" means stretch.
Get it wrong yourself now and then, big and silly, so your kid can catch you.

activities.title: Room Train
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who knows the rooms by name and a parent who can be an engine for ten minutes.
steps: Be the engine, with your kid holding on behind you, and chug round the house with a "choo choo".
Pull into a station, stop, and ask "where next?", and they name a room.
Chug off to that room, stop there, and swap so they drive and you call the stations.

activities.title: Pop and Flop
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who knows one song by heart and a parent who can flop onto a cushion and get up again.
steps: Pick a song with a surprise word, like the pop in Pop Goes the Weasel, and march round the room singing it.
On the surprise word, both of you flop onto the cushions, then get up and march on.
Sing slower and slower as the word gets close, so the wait for the flop gets longer.

activities.title: Banana Kick
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more with a soft ball, and a parent who can fetch it from under the sofa.
steps: Put a soft ball at your kid's feet and agree the magic word is "banana".
Say other foods slowly, "apple, carrot, cheese", and they wait with still feet until "banana" means kick.
Run after the ball together, set it back, and let them call the foods while you wait to kick.

activities.title: Round the Sofa
activities.blurb: Good for a sofa you can get all the way round, and a kid of 2 and up who runs laps whether you join in or not.
steps: Jog slow laps round the sofa together, your kid just ahead of you.
Call "switch" and both of you stop, turn round, and run the other way.
Switch sooner and sooner, then let your kid call it and try to catch you turning late.

activities.title: Three Sock Hunt
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who can count a little and a parent who can dash round a room hiding socks.
steps: Send your kid to the wall to count to ten out loud while you dash round hiding three socks in easy spots.
They hunt, carry each sock back to the cup one at a time, and you ask "how many more?" after each one.
Swap, so they hide three while you count out loud, and they tell you how many are still out.

activities.title: Sleepy Animals
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who lies still for a count of five if a hop is coming, and a parent who hops.
steps: Lie down on the cushions together, eyes shut, and whisper "we are sleeping frogs".
Stay still for a slow count of five, then shout "wake up" and both hop like frogs to the far wall and back.
Lie down again and whisper a new animal, and from about two let your kid choose it.

activities.title: Carry the Word
activities.blurb: Good for a talker of 2 and up, a hallway, and a parent who does not mind "pancake" shouted ten times.
steps: Stand at one end of the hallway with your kid and whisper a word to them, like "pancake".
They run to the far end, shout the word back to you, and run home for the next one.
When one word is easy, give two, and take your turn running and shouting while they choose the words.

activities.title: Singing Carpet
activities.blurb: Good for a smooth floor, a blanket, and a kid of 2 and up who will sing for a ride.
steps: Sit your kid in the middle of a blanket on a smooth floor and take hold of two corners.
The carpet only moves while they sing, so pull slowly as the song goes and stop the moment it stops.
Call "rocks ahead" now and then, so they have to stop singing to stop the carpet.

activities.title: Sock on Me
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who loves to search you, one sock, and a parent who can dodge round the room a bit.
steps: Turn your back, tuck a rolled sock somewhere on you, under an arm, in a pocket, under a foot, and turn round.
Dance about the room while your kid chases you to find it, and stop so they can search when they catch you.
Hide it somewhere new each round and ask "where was it last time?" before they look.

activities.title: Tug and Stop
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who pulls at everything, one towel, and a parent who can lose on purpose.
steps: Hold one end of a towel and give your kid the other, and both pull as hard as you can.
Say "stop" and both let the towel go slack, hands still holding on, for a slow count of three.
Say "pull" to start again, and let your kid be the one who says stop.

activities.title: Copy My Path
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who likes to get it right, three cushions, and a parent who can hop.
steps: Lay out three cushions and hop onto two of them, one after the other, naming each as you land.
Let your kid hop the same two in the same order, and if they stall, ask "where next?" instead of pointing.
Swap, so they hop a path and you copy it, saying out loud where you are going.

activities.title: Cushion Nest
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who carries cushions about anyway, and a parent who can carry the big ones.
steps: Say "let's build a nest in the corner" and carry the first cushion over together.
Let your kid carry the rest one at a time, and when they stop, ask "what next?" rather than fetching one.
Climb into the nest together as two birds and tweet, then take it apart cushion by cushion.

activities.title: Knock at Every Door
activities.blurb: Good for a home with a few rooms, a kid of 2 and up who runs between them, and a parent who can keep up.
steps: Run from room to room together, but every doorway is a gate where you must stop.
Knock three times on the frame, say the room's name, and only then run through.
Speed up the running, keep the knocks slow, and let your kid say the names first.

activities.title: Name the Chaser
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who wants to chase and be chased in the same minute, and a parent up for both.
steps: Say "I chase" and chase your kid round the room with big slow steps.
Call "you chase" and swap on the spot, so now you run away and they chase.
Swap faster and faster, and stop everything the moment anyone says "stop".

activities.title: Bear Hunt Walk
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who loves a story they can march through, and a whole home to roam.
steps: March round the house on a bear hunt, swishing through grass, splashing a river and squelching through mud.
In the last room spot the bear, gasp, and run home back through the mud, then the river, then the grass.
Hide under a blanket together and whisper "we are not going on a bear hunt again".

activities.title: Bridge Falls Down
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who runs in circles anyway, one song you both know, and a squeeze at the end.
steps: Lean on the wall with both hands to make a bridge, and sing London Bridge while your kid runs under and back.
Drop your arms on the last word and catch your kid in a squeeze if they are still underneath.
Sing faster or slower each time so nobody can guess when the bridge will fall.

activities.title: Lights Out
activities.blurb: Good for the last noisy stretch before bed with a kid of 2 and up, when roaring must turn into whispering.
steps: Stand by the light switch while your kid runs and roars around the room.
Flick the light off, and in the dark everyone freezes and whispers "shhh" until the light is back.
Lift your kid up to work the switch, and freeze and whisper when they plunge you into the dark.

activities.title: Cloud Catch
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more, a scarf, and a parent who can throw it to the ceiling a dozen times.
steps: Throw a scarf or small towel high in the air and call "sky", so your kid catches it before it lands.
Throw again and call "floor", so now they wait with hands behind their back until it lands, then stamp on it.
Mix the two calls and throw higher each time, then give them a turn to throw while you catch or wait.

activities.title: Creep Up on Me
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who loves sneaking, and a parent who can spin round and chase.
steps: Stand at one end of the room facing the wall while your kid creeps up behind you from the other end.
Turn round whenever you like, and they must freeze, so anyone caught moving tiptoes back to the start.
When they tap your back, chase them back to the start with a roar, then face the wall again.

activities.title: Sock Rain
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who throws everything, a cup of rolled socks, and a room that ends up tidy.
steps: Tip a cup of rolled socks on the floor and shout "rain", so both of you throw them up as high as you can.
Shout "sunshine" and all throwing stops, and now every sock goes back in the cup as fast as you can.
Rain and sunshine again until you are puffed, and the last sunshine leaves the socks tidied away.

activities.title: Slowest Wins
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who gets the joke, and a parent who wants a race without the sprint.
steps: Line up at the wall and say "ready, steady, go", but in this race the slowest one across the room wins.
Walk like you are wading through honey, and anyone who speeds up goes back to the wall.
When your kid has the hang of it, race once where fastest wins, then swap back to slowest.

activities.title: Hungry Sofa
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who likes to sort, a pile of socks and blocks, and a parent who runs too.
steps: Say the sofa is hungry for socks and the chair across the room is hungry for blocks.
Tip a mixed pile of socks and blocks in the middle, and run each one to the right eater together.
When the pile is gone, swap the menus, so now the sofa wants blocks, and go again.

activities.title: Sock Says
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of two or more who already ignores you, a sock, and a parent with a puppet voice.
steps: Put a sock on your hand as a puppet, and only the puppet gives orders, like "jump" or "run to the door".
When your own voice says "jump", nobody jumps, so look sad and ask the puppet to say it.
Do every order along with your kid, then give them the sock and obey only their puppet.

activities.title: Run and Stack
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who builds towers and knocks them down, and a parent who can run for a block.
steps: Pile the cups or blocks at one end of the room and stand together at the other.
Take turns, so one of you runs for a piece and places it on the tower while the other waits at the line.
If the tower falls, both run to rebuild it fast, then back to slow careful turns.

activities.title: Whisper Chase
activities.blurb: Good for a chase when someone else is asleep, and a kid of 2 and up who squeals at the sight of you.
steps: Whisper "I'm coming to get you" and chase your kid round the room, everything in whispers.
If anyone squeals or shouts, you both sit on the floor for a whispered count of three, then start again.
Swap chasers, and stop the game the moment either of you says "stop".

activities.title: Run Home
activities.blurb: Good for two cushions, a kid of 2 and up who loves a race to a spot, and a parent who can lose the race.
steps: Give each of you a home cushion in a different corner, then wander the room doing silly walks.
Shout "home" and both race to sit on your own cushion.
Swap homes every few rounds, and cheer when you both remember which cushion is yours now.

activities.title: Find the Song
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who stops to listen when music plays, and a parent who can crawl under the table.
steps: Play a song quietly on your phone and tuck it behind a cushion while your kid covers their eyes.
Say "find the song" and crawl round the room with them, stopping to listen whenever they stop.
Hide it somewhere new each time, further away and quieter.

activities.title: Cat and Mouse
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who pounces on everything, one rolled sock, and a parent on the floor for a bit.
steps: Wiggle a rolled sock along the floor as a mouse, and your kid is the cat, crawling after it.
The cat may only pounce when the mouse stops moving, so wiggle it, stop, and wait for them.
Swap, so they wiggle the mouse and you are a big slow cat who pounces only when it stops.

activities.title: High Five Hunt
activities.blurb: Good for five minutes with nothing in your hands, and a kid of 2 and up who will run anywhere for a high five.
steps: Hold your hand out flat somewhere new each time, high, low, behind your knee, and your kid runs to slap it.
Close your hand into a fist, and a fist means wait, so they stand still until it opens.
Walk about the room between fives so they chase the hand, then hold yours out for them to find.

activities.title: Step in My Steps
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of 2 and up who watches your feet, and a parent who can take big silly steps.
steps: Take three big slow steps across the floor, stamping each one so your kid sees exactly where your feet land.
They follow, putting their feet only where yours were, and you cheer every landing.
Add a sideways step or a hop, then follow their steps across the room.

activities.title: Swap Hands
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a cup with a sock in it, and a kid of 2 and up who can walk and listen at once.
steps: Walk the hallway together, each carrying a cup with a rolled sock in it, in your right hands.
Call "swap" and both cups move to the other hand without stopping and without a sock falling out.
Call it sooner and sooner, then let your kid call the swaps and jog a little between them.

activities.title: Rescue Teddy
activities.blurb: Good for a teddy stuck on the sofa, a floor of cushions, and a kid of 2 and up who likes a plan.
steps: Put teddy up on the sofa and say he is stuck, then plan a two part rescue, like "over the cushion, then up".
Say the two parts together, then crawl and climb the plan side by side to reach him.
Put teddy somewhere new and let your kid tell you the two parts before anyone moves.

activities.title: Human Mountain
activities.blurb: Good for climbing, giggles, and a parent who needs to lie down.
steps: Lie on your back on the rug as a sleeping mountain.
Your kid climbs while you narrate the expedition in a whisper.
At the summit the mountain rumbles, then you start again.

activities.title: Sleepy Lion
activities.blurb: Good for sneaking, roaring, and a parent who can play with their eyes shut.
steps: You are a lion asleep on the sofa, snoring loudly.
Your kid sneaks up, and if you hear a sound you open one eye.
When they touch your paw you wake up roaring, then swap roles.

activities.title: Three-Word Story
activities.blurb: Good for the sofa, a tired voice, and a dragon that goes wherever you say.
steps: Start every story with "Once, a tiny dragon" and take turns adding exactly three words.
Count the words on your fingers, so nobody slips in a fourth.
The last turn has to end the story, then a new dragon starts.

activities.title: Switch Spy
activities.blurb: Good for a cluttered living room, a kid who loves to be right, and a parent glued to the sofa.
steps: Say "I spy something red" and your kid finds it from where you sit.
After three colours switch the clue to shapes, like "I spy something round", then to what things are for.
Swap so they spy and you guess, and they choose when the clue type switches.

activities.title: Day Says Night
activities.blurb: Good for three and a half and up, a dim room, and a parent who can talk but not move.
steps: When you say "day" your kid answers "night", and when you say "night" they answer "day".
Start slow, then speed up until one of you slips.
Add a second pair like hot and cold, and let them quiz you back.

activities.title: Whisper Telephone
activities.blurb: Good for a sleeping sibling next door, a snuggly kid, and a parent whose voice is gone.
steps: Whisper a short message into your kid's ear, like "the cat ate a sock".
They whisper it back into your ear, word for word.
Each round add one more word to the message, and swap who sends it.

activities.title: What's Missing
activities.blurb: Good for a sofa covered in toys, a sharp eyed kid, and a parent who only has to lift one thing.
steps: Line up four toys on the sofa arm and name them together.
Your kid shuts their eyes while you slide one toy under a cushion.
They open their eyes and name the missing toy, then add a fifth toy and swap.

activities.title: Sofa Shopping
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who needs a mission, a house full of stuff, and a parent who stays horizontal.
steps: Order three things from around the house, like a spoon, a sock and a blue book.
Your kid says the list back, then fetches all three in one trip.
Check what came back and in what order, then make the next list one thing longer.

activities.title: Stop at Four
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who counts everything, a dark bedroom, and a parent who can manage ten numbers.
steps: Pick a secret stop number together, like four.
Count down from ten out loud together, and both of you go silent on the stop number.
Whoever says it by mistake picks the next stop number.

activities.title: Belly Boat
activities.blurb: Good for winding down, a wound up kid, and a parent who was going to lie here anyway.
steps: Lie on your backs with a small toy riding on each belly.
Breathe in slowly so the boat rises, then out slowly so it sinks.
Count five boat rides together, then watch one more without a word.

activities.title: Yes Means No
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who loves being cheeky, a parked car, and a parent with questions but no legs.
steps: Ask easy questions like "is this a sock?" and your kid must give the opposite answer.
Any truthful answer ends their turn, and after five questions you swap.
Make the questions sillier as you go, so the wrong answer gets harder to find.

activities.title: Tell It Back
activities.blurb: Good for the last book of the night, a kid who knows it by heart, and a parent who can only ask.
steps: Read one short book, or tell a story your kid knows well.
Close it and ask "what happened first?", then "and then?" until the end.
Peek at the pages together to fix any muddled order.

activities.title: Rhyme Chain
activities.blurb: Good for a chatty kid, a traffic jam, and a parent who can rhyme with their eyes shut.
steps: Say a word like "cat" and your kid answers with a rhyme.
Take turns adding rhymes, and a rhyme already said is out.
When someone is stuck they say "pop" and pick the next word.

activities.title: Pack for the Moon
activities.blurb: Good for a kid with big plans, a sofa that is also a rocket, and a parent who only has to steer.
steps: Decide together where the pretend trip goes, like the moon.
Your kid says what to pack in order, then mimes putting each thing into an invisible suitcase.
Fly there on the sofa, then unpack the suitcase in the same order and see what got forgotten.

activities.title: Clap or Tap
activities.blurb: Good for a four year old who wants a hard one, and a parent who can say words from a pillow.
steps: Say words one at a time: for an animal your kid claps, for a colour they tap their knees.
Mix in words that are neither, like "spoon", which get nothing at all.
After ten words swap the rules, so animals tap and colours clap.

activities.title: Frozen Face
activities.blurb: Good for a hand mirror, a kid who cannot stop giggling, and a parent who can do a face.
steps: Pull a silly face into the mirror together.
Say "freeze" and both of you hold the face for a count of five without a giggle.
Each round the count grows by one, and whoever melts first counts next.

activities.title: Which Hand
activities.blurb: Good for one sock, a kid of four and up who hates waiting, and a parent who hides things behind their back.
steps: Hide a rolled up sock in one fist behind your back, then show both fists.
Before your kid may point, sing one line of a song together.
They tap a fist and you open it, and after three goes you swap.

activities.title: Five Sounds
activities.blurb: Good for the quietest half hour of the day, a buzzing kid, and a parent who wants silence too.
steps: Lie still together with your eyes shut and listen.
Each time one of you hears a sound, whisper what it was and hold up a finger.
Stop at five fingers, then decide together which sound was the quietest.

activities.title: Three Kind Things
activities.blurb: Good for the end of a rough day, a kid who needs a soft landing, and a parent lying beside them.
steps: Ask your kid for three kind things that happened today, done by them or for them.
Count them on their fingers and ask who each one helped.
Tell them your three, and pick together one kind thing for tomorrow.

activities.title: Melting Snowman
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who is too wound up to sleep, and a parent who only needs a slow voice.
steps: Your kid lies down as a frozen snowman, stiff from toes to nose.
Name one body part at a time, and the sun melts it soft into the floor.
When the whole snowman is a puddle, breathe out together and freeze it again.

activities.title: Spot the Change
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who notices everything, and a parent who can take off a sock without getting up.
steps: Your kid studies you for a count of ten, then hides their eyes.
Change one thing about yourself, like a sock gone or a cushion on your head.
They look again and name the change, then they change something and you guess.

activities.title: Rewind the Day
activities.blurb: Good for lights out, a kid who likes to talk about their day, and a parent who only has to ask.
steps: Start with right now and ask "and before that?" to walk the day backwards.
Give a hint only when your kid stalls, and keep going until breakfast.
Next round rewind a story you both know, from the end back to the beginning.

activities.title: I Saw a Zebra
activities.blurb: Good for a long wait, a kid who knows a lot of animals, and a parent who can count on fingers.
steps: Say "I went to the zoo and saw a zebra".
Your kid repeats the whole list and adds one animal, then you do the same.
Keep going until someone drops an animal, then start a new trip to a new place.

activities.title: Three Clues
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who blurts out answers, a parked car, and a parent who knows a few animals.
steps: Give three clues about an animal, like "it is grey, it is huge, it has a trunk".
Your kid holds their guess in until all three clues are said, then says it.
They give you three clues next, and you wait the same way.

activities.title: Ear Hands
activities.blurb: Good for a picture book, a kid who wants to be the reader, and a parent happy to say nothing.
steps: Your kid holds the book and tells the story from the pictures.
You cup your hands behind your ears as the listener and do not say one word until the last page.
Then swap, so you read and they wear the ear hands.

activities.title: Torch Trail
activities.blurb: Good for a dim room, a kid who loves the torch, and a parent who only moves a thumb.
steps: Dim the room and shine the phone torch on three things, one after another.
Switch it off and your kid names the three things in the same order.
Add a fourth thing, then hand over the torch so they can test you.

activities.title: Towel Surprise
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who cannot wait for anything, a towel, and a parent who counts slowly.
steps: Wrap a toy in a towel behind your back while your kid faces away.
Set it on your lap and they wait while you count slowly to twenty, no peeking and no touching.
Ask what helped them wait, like singing or looking away, and use it next round with a longer count.

activities.title: Spoon Bell
activities.blurb: Good for snack time, a kid who grabs, and a parent slumped at the table with a spoon.
steps: Put one bite of their snack under a cup while your kid sits with hands flat on the table.
They may lift the cup only when the spoon taps the cup like a bell.
Make each wait a little longer, and sometimes lift the spoon without tapping.

activities.title: Sofa Doctor
activities.blurb: Good for a parent who really is poorly on the sofa, and a kid who takes charge.
steps: You are the patient in bed with a very silly illness, like hiccups in your knees.
Your kid is the doctor who must check your ears, your heart and your toes, in that order, before the cure.
Next round the teddy is the patient, and your kid tells you which three checks come first.

activities.title: Wrong Word
activities.blurb: Good for a book you have read a hundred times, and a kid who corrects you anyway.
steps: Read a book your kid knows by heart.
On some pages swap one word for a wrong one, like "the cat wore a boat".
They say "stop" and fix it, and the pages with no mistake are the real test.

activities.title: Eyes Shut Claps
activities.blurb: Good for a kid learning to count, a dark room, and a parent who can clap behind a cushion.
steps: Your kid shuts their eyes while you clap a few times behind a cushion.
They hold up that many fingers, and you show the answer with yours.
Mix slow claps with quick ones to make counting harder, then swap.

activities.title: Missing Word Song
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of four and up who knows all the words, and a parent who can sing lying down.
steps: Sing a song you both know, like "Twinkle Twinkle".
Pick one word, like "star", and every time it comes you both clap instead of singing it.
Each round add one more silent word.

activities.title: What Next Coach
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who says "you do it", and a parent whose hands are staying under the blanket.
steps: Set a building challenge, like a tower taller than the cup with a bridge for the teddy.
Your kid builds while your hands stay under the blanket, and you only ask "what next?" or "what if?".
When it falls, ask what they will change, and watch round two.

activities.title: Squeeze Code
activities.blurb: Good for holding hands in the dark, a kid who likes secrets, and a parent who can squeeze.
steps: Agree a code: one squeeze of the hand means wiggle your toes, two means stick out your tongue.
Your kid shuts their eyes and does whatever your squeezes say.
Add a three squeeze move, then swap so they send and you do.

activities.title: Pretend Phone
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who does voices, and a parent who can hold a hand to their ear.
steps: Ring your kid on a hand phone and say who is calling, like Grandma or a hungry wolf.
They answer in that caller's voice and keep it up until you hang up.
Ring again as someone new every minute, then they call you.

activities.title: Sofa Captain
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who likes orders, a messy room, and a parent who navigates from the sofa.
steps: Spot a toy across the room and give a route in three moves, like "two steps, turn left, crawl under".
Your kid repeats the route, then follows it exactly to the toy.
Make the next route four moves, then let them captain your hand along the sofa.

activities.title: Tree and Rock
activities.blurb: Good for a kid with wobbly energy left, and a parent who counts breaths from the sofa.
steps: Your kid stands as a tree on one leg while you count five slow breaths together.
Say "rock" and they curl up small and still for five more breaths.
Switch between tree and rock on your word, and let them pick a third pose that you do sitting down.

activities.title: Plan Then Play
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who plays beside you anyway, and a parent who wants to join from the sofa.
steps: Before your kid plays, they tell you the plan in three parts, like "teddy cooks, the cars crash, then bath".
Say the plan back to them, and they play it out beside you.
After five minutes ask which parts happened and what changed.

activities.title: Statue Hide
activities.blurb: Good for hide and seek when you cannot get up, and a kid who can hold a giggle in.
steps: Shut your eyes on the sofa and count to ten while your kid hides somewhere in the room.
Without moving, guess out loud, like "are you behind the chair?".
They stay still and silent until a right guess, then they count and you hide under the blanket.

activities.title: Say Then Do
activities.blurb: Good for a kid whose hands move before their head, a teddy, and a parent who watches.
steps: Give your kid a job, like dressing the teddy in two socks and a scarf.
The rule is they say each step out loud before their hands move, like "now the left sock".
If the hands go first, the teddy undresses and the job starts again.

activities.title: True Ball
activities.blurb: Good for a ball, a kid who catches everything, and a parent who can roll from the sofa.
steps: Roll the ball to your kid and say something true or false, like "cows can fly".
They catch it only when it is true, and let a false one roll straight past.
Swap after five rolls, and get sillier.

activities.title: Hum That Tune
activities.blurb: Good for a late evening, a kid of four and up who knows ten songs, and a parent who can hum with eyes shut.
steps: Hum a song your kid knows, mouth shut and no words.
They guess it, and only then do you both sing the first line.
Swap, and the hummer has to stay humming even when the guesser gets close.

activities.title: Finger Fibber
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who counts to ten, and a parent who can lie about it from the floor.
steps: Hold up some fingers and say a different number out loud, like three fingers and "five".
Your kid says the number of fingers they see, not the number they hear.
Swap after ten goes, and try to catch each other out.

activities.title: Invisible Box
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who loves charades, and a parent whose hands are the only moving parts.
steps: Open a pretend box on your chest and mime pulling out one thing, like licking an ice cream.
Your kid guesses it, then pulls out the next thing for you to guess.
The box only holds things from one place, like the kitchen, and the place changes every round.

activities.title: Turn Tower
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who grabs all the blocks, and a parent who is in no hurry.
steps: Build one tower together, one block each, strictly taking turns.
Your turn is slow on purpose, and your kid's hands stay in their lap until you say "your turn".
When it falls, whoever placed the last block starts the new one.

activities.title: One Word Each
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of four and up who sings over you, and a parent with one word at a time left.
steps: Sing a song you both know, but only one word each, taking turns.
Nobody may sing two words in a row, even on the best bit.
Then try two words each, and then back to one.

activities.title: Dragon Clap
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who drifts off during stories, and a parent who can make one up lying down.
steps: Make up a story, and every time it says "dragon" your kid claps once.
Slip in "dragonfly" and "wagon" to tempt a wrong clap.
Halfway through, change the clap word to "cake" and keep going.

activities.title: Back Drawing
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who likes a back rub, bedtime, and a parent who can move one finger.
steps: Your kid lies on their tummy and you draw a shape on their back slowly with one finger.
They say what it was, like a circle, a zigzag or a letter from their name.
Then they draw on your back, and you keep your eyes shut while you guess.

activities.title: Answer Drum
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who copies everything, and a parent tapping the sofa arm.
steps: Tap a short rhythm on the sofa arm, like a question.
Your kid taps back an answer that has to be different from yours.
Keep the conversation going without ever copying each other, then swap who asks.

activities.title: Rusty Robot
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who wants to be the boss, and a parent who moves one thumb at a time.
steps: You are a rusty robot who moves one body part per order, like "left thumb".
Your kid gives the orders, and a part already used makes the robot buzz and break down.
Count how many orders they manage before a repeat, then swap.

activities.title: Guess My Rule
activities.blurb: Good for a sock pile, a kid who likes detective work, and a parent sorting from the sofa.
steps: Sort the socks into two piles by a secret rule, like stripes and plain.
Your kid watches and calls out the rule as soon as they spot it.
They sort by their own secret rule and you guess, and no rule may be used twice.

activities.title: Gap Clap
activities.blurb: Good for four and up, a kid who claps along to everything, and a parent keeping a slow beat.
steps: Clap a slow steady beat, like a clock.
Your kid claps only in the gaps between your claps, never with them.
Speed up a little each round, then swap.

activities.title: Hands in Lap
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who grabs first, three toys, and a parent who can hold them out of reach.
steps: Hold out three toys, and your kid chooses one with words only, hands in their lap.
Hand it over only after a full sentence, like "I would like the red car, please".
Then they hold the toys and you choose, with your hands under the blanket.

activities.title: Eyes Shut Map
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who knows the room by heart and a parent who is not leaving the sofa.
steps: Your kid looks round the room for a slow count of ten, then shuts their eyes tight.
Ask "where is the lamp?" and they point to it with eyes shut, then the door, then the window.
Swap over, and they pick three things for you to find blind.

activities.title: Teddy's Password
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who forgets what you said a minute ago and a parent lying flat under a blanket.
steps: Whisper a password to your kid, like "purple elephant", and warn them the teddy guard will ask for it.
Sing one whole song together, or tell a short story, and nobody mentions the password.
Then the teddy on your chest asks "password?" and lets them climb up only for the right words.

activities.title: Twins
activities.blurb: Good for a dark bedroom, a kid who loves catching you out, and a parent whose eyes are already shut.
steps: Say animals one at a time, slowly, like "cow, duck, duck, pig".
Your kid calls "twins" only when an animal is the same as the one right before it.
Swap over, so your kid calls the animals and tries to sneak the twins past you.

activities.title: Toe Names
activities.blurb: Good for bedtime, bare feet, and a parent who can reach a foot without sitting up.
steps: Name each of your kid's toes after a food, like Pizza, Banana, Soup, Cheese and Egg, and say them twice.
Your kid shuts their eyes while you wiggle one toe, and they tell you its name.
Then your kid names your toes and wiggles one, and it is your turn to remember.

activities.title: Don't Say It
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who knows every toy in the house and a parent who can play with eyes half shut.
steps: Pick a toy in the room in your head and describe it without saying its name or its colour.
Your kid guesses it from the sofa, then picks one and describes it for you.
Any slip, like "the red car", hands the turn straight back to the other player.

activities.title: Colour Not Name
activities.blurb: Good for a bright room full of stuff and a parent who only has to lift a finger.
steps: Point at things round the room, and your kid says only the colour, never the name, so the cup is "blue".
Go faster and faster, and the first time a name slips out, like "cup", you swap jobs.

activities.title: Just a Picture
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who wants the toy right now and a parent lying flat with a trick up their sleeve.
steps: Set a toy they love on the cushion beside you and frame it with your fingers, so now it is only a picture.
Nobody touches a picture, so while the frame is up you both describe it like a painting in a museum.
Drop the frame after a slow count of ten, and the toy turns real and theirs.

activities.title: Sneeze Number
activities.blurb: Good for the car, a waiting room or the sofa, and a kid who can count to ten.
steps: Count to ten taking turns, but the number four has a cold, so whoever lands on it says "achoo" instead.
Anyone who says "four" out loud sends the count back to one.
Once it is easy, give the cold to a different number, like seven.

activities.title: Odd One Out, Twice
activities.blurb: Good for the car, the sofa or the bath, and a kid who loves being right.
steps: Say three things, like "apple, banana, red car", and your kid picks the odd one out and says why.
Then ask for a different odd one with a different reason, like the banana because it is not red.
Swap, and they give you three things to puzzle over.

activities.title: Twist Button
activities.blurb: Good for a bedtime story gone stale and a kid who loves it when things go wrong.
steps: Tell a story you both know, and your nose is the twist button your kid may press at any time.
Every press means the next thing in the story must change, like the wolf shrinking to the size of a pea.
Swap over, so your kid tells and you press, and every twist stays in the story to the end.

activities.title: Tuck In Swap
activities.blurb: Good for a parent already in bed and a kid who has waited all day to be the boss.
steps: Your kid is the parent and you are the kid, so they tuck you in, read one page and tell you to sleep.
Whenever either of you says "swap", you switch roles and carry on from that exact moment.
The game ends when the kid, whoever that is by then, is tucked in and quiet.

activities.title: Word Station
activities.blurb: Good for a dark room, two tired voices, and no hands needed at all.
steps: Take turns saying fruits, one each, like a train picking up passengers at the fruit station.
When you call "new station", the train takes animals instead, and a fruit said now stops the train.
Your kid calls the next station, like colours or things in the kitchen.

activities.title: Sound Detective
activities.blurb: Good for a quiet evening, a kid who loves a mystery, and a parent who only has to tap things.
steps: Put a cup, a book and a toy in front of your kid and tap each one on the floor so they hear its sound.
They shut their eyes, you tap one, and they point to the thing that made the noise.
Add a fourth thing after three right answers in a row, then swap so you are the detective.

activities.title: Tune Switch
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of four and up, a bedroom with the lights off, and a parent who can hum but cannot get up.
steps: Hum a song your kid knows, like "Twinkle Twinkle", with no words.
Slide into a different song without stopping, and your kid raises a hand the moment the tune changes.
Swap, and try to catch their switch.

activities.title: Ceiling Cinema
activities.blurb: Good for lying on your backs in the dark and a kid who sees things that are not there.
steps: Lie on your backs and tell your kid a tiny dragon is flying about the ceiling, saying exactly where it goes.
Your kid's finger points to where the dragon is at every moment, from the lamp to the corner to the door.
Swap, so your kid flies the dragon with words and your finger follows.

activities.title: Silent Ten
activities.blurb: Good for the last few minutes before sleep and a kid who is still a little bit loud.
steps: Both hide your hands under the blanket and count to ten on your fingers without one sound.
Clap once the moment you reach ten, trying to land on the exact same clap as each other.
Next round count to twenty, and whisper afterwards who got there first.

activities.title: Swap Story
activities.blurb: Good for lights out, a kid who loves to interrupt, and a parent who only has to keep talking.
steps: Start a made up story, and agree that a tap on the nose means the other person takes over mid sentence.
Whoever gets tapped carries on from the exact word where the story stopped.
Tap more often as you go, until you are swapping every few words.

activities.title: Sock Hunt
activities.blurb: Good for a messy sock drawer, a kid of four and up who loves to seek, and a parent who hides sitting down.
steps: Roll five socks into balls and hide them while your kid counts to twenty with eyes shut.
Say "warm" or "cold" as they search, and count the finds out loud.
Swap, so your kid hides and you hunt from your chair with their clues.

activities.title: Mirror, Mirror
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who loves being watched and a parent who can stand up but not much more.
steps: Face each other, your kid moves and you copy them as slowly as you can.
Make it harder with faces, then sounds, then silly walks on the spot.
Swap who leads every two minutes, and the leader goes slower each time.

activities.title: Pillow Islands
activities.blurb: Good for a floor full of cushions and a parent who would rather be the lifeguard than swim.
steps: Lay the cushions across the floor as islands, and the floor is the sea.
Your kid crosses the room island to island without touching the water.
Each time they make it across, you take one island away.

activities.title: Simon Says
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who moves anyway and a parent who can give orders from the sofa.
steps: Call out moves, and your kid only does the ones that start with "Simon says".
Mix in plain orders like "touch your nose" and catch them if they move.
After three catches your kid is Simon and you follow.

activities.title: Bear and Dragon
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who adores puppets and a parent with two spare socks and two silly voices.
steps: Put a sock on each hand, one a kind bear with a soft voice and one a grumpy dragon with a growl.
Your kid does whatever the bear asks and never what the dragon orders.
Let the dragon ask for the fun things, like a jump, to make saying no hard.

activities.title: Heads Mean Toes
activities.blurb: Good for a kid of four and up who knows their body parts, and a parent who can call them out from a chair.
steps: Tell your kid that when you say "head" they touch their toes, and when you say "toes" they touch their head.
Call the two words in a random order, slowly at first and then faster.
Add knees and shoulders as a second swapped pair when the first is easy.

activities.title: Purple Light
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a kid who loves to go, and a parent who stands at the finish line.
steps: Stand at one end, and your kid walks toward you on "purple light" and freezes on "red light".
When they reach you, swap the words, so now red means go and purple means stop.
Call the colours faster each round, and whoever wobbles goes back to the start.

activities.title: Colour Match Freeze
activities.blurb: Good for one song, a pile of odd socks, and a parent who can hold a sock up from the sofa.
steps: Put on a song, and your kid dances while you hold a handful of different coloured socks.
Stop the music and hold up one sock, so your kid runs to touch something that colour and freezes there.
Start the music again, and the next sock is a new colour.

activities.title: Cup Drum Walk
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who marches anyway and a parent who can tap a spoon on an upturned cup.
steps: Tap a spoon on an upturned cup, and your kid walks one step for every beat, fast or slow as you play.
Change the speed without warning and see how fast their feet catch up.
Now flip it, so fast beats mean slow steps and slow beats mean fast feet.

activities.title: The Conductor
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who claps for everything and a parent conducting from the armchair.
steps: Hold your hands high for loud claps and low for soft ones, and your kid claps along.
Close your fist for silence, and open it to start again.
Swap, so your kid conducts with their hands and you clap, obeying every move.

activities.title: Clap Echo
activities.blurb: Good for a kitchen chair, a kid who copies everything, and a parent with just their hands.
steps: Clap a short pattern, and your kid claps it straight back.
Add one clap each round, and mix slow and quick ones.
When they miss, your kid makes the patterns and you echo.

activities.title: Sock Sort Switch
activities.blurb: Good for laundry day, a kid who likes piles, and a parent sorting from the floor.
steps: Tip out the socks, and your kid sorts them by colour onto two cushions, dark here and light there.
Once the pile is gone, mix them up and switch the rule to size, big socks here and small socks there.
Call "switch" halfway through a pile for a real test.

activities.title: Cup Shuffle
activities.blurb: Good for the kitchen table, a kid of four and up with sharp eyes, and a parent who can slide three cups.
steps: Turn three cups upside down and hide a sock ball under one while your kid watches.
Slide two cups past each other slowly, then swap another pair, and ask which cup hides the sock.
Add a swap each round, then hand over the cups so your kid shuffles and you guess.

activities.title: Build My Plan
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who builds and a parent who would rather describe a tower than stack it.
steps: Describe a tower in words first, like three cups, then the book, then two cups on top.
Your kid builds it from memory while you keep your hands in your lap.
Check it together against the plan, then your kid describes one and you build.

activities.title: Five Breath Zoo
activities.blurb: Good for a wound up kid who likes animals and a parent who can stand still.
steps: Pick an animal shape, like a tall giraffe on tiptoes or a frog crouched low, and both of you hold it.
Count five slow breaths out loud while nobody wobbles or talks.
Your kid picks the next animal, and the poses get harder each round.

activities.title: Pretend Restaurant
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who loves to serve and a parent who can sit at a table and be fussy.
steps: Sit down as the customer and order three dishes, like soup, a pizza and a banana.
Your kid the waiter repeats the order back, then cooks it from cushions and cups.
They serve the three dishes in the order you asked, and the next round you add a drink.

activities.title: Opposite Day
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who thinks rules are funny and a parent who can call them out from a chair.
steps: Today "walk" means stop and "stop" means walk, so say them and watch your kid do the opposite.
Add "loud" for whispering and "quiet" for shouting.
Whoever gets three right in a row makes up the next pair of opposites.

activities.title: Sculptor and Statue
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who can stand still for a dare and a parent who moves slowly anyway.
steps: Your kid is the clay, so gently move an arm here and a leg there into a pose.
Walk slowly round your statue pulling faces while it holds perfectly still.
Swap, and your kid sculpts you into something ridiculous.

activities.title: Less Is More
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who always wants the big pile and a parent who can count socks sitting down.
steps: Make two piles of sock balls, one with two socks and one with five.
Tell them the rule, the pile they point to goes to you and the other pile is theirs.
Count what each of you got, then mix the piles and try again.

activities.title: Closed Hands
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who cannot wait and a parent with a small toy in a pocket.
steps: Your kid shuts their eyes and holds out two closed hands.
Count slowly to twenty together, and if their eyes or hands open you start the count again.
At twenty, a small toy lands in their hands, and next round the count grows by five.

activities.title: Book Detective
activities.blurb: Good for the sofa, a kid who knows every page, and a parent who can point.
steps: Open any picture book and ask your kid to find something red on the page.
Next ask for something round, then for something that is both red and round.
Swap, so your kid picks the clue and you search.

activities.title: Slow Tightrope
activities.blurb: Good for a hallway, a kid with good balance, and a parent who claps from the end.
steps: Lay a scarf or towel flat along the floor as the tightrope.
Your kid walks it heel to toe as slowly as they can, and the slowest crossing wins.
Add a sock ball balanced on their head for the next crossing.

activities.title: Whisper Orders
activities.blurb: Good for a sleeping sibling, a loud kid, and a parent who is done with noise.
steps: Whisper a silly order in your kid's ear, like hop to the door and back.
They do it and whisper back what they did, and any loud voice costs a turn.
Swap, and your kid whispers the orders.

activities.title: Floor Map Journey
activities.blurb: Good for a room with cushions, a kid who loves adventures, and a parent who stays at base camp.
steps: The floor is a map, so cushions are mountains, a scarf is a river and the sofa is the castle.
Plan the route out loud together, like river, then mountains, then castle, before anyone moves.
Your kid travels the whole route from memory, then plans a new one for you.

activities.title: Three Moves
activities.blurb: Good for a kid who copies everything and a parent who can show a move sitting down.
steps: Show three moves in a row, like a jump, a toe touch and a clap.
Your kid does all three in the same order, and if they get it, add a fourth.
Now ask for the same moves backwards.

activities.title: Turtle and Rabbit
activities.blurb: Good for a kitchen table, a kid with a crayon, and a parent who does the voices.
steps: Your kid draws a line across the page as slowly as a turtle while you count.
Say "rabbit" and the line races to the edge, then "turtle" and it crawls again.
Switch animals halfway along a line, and give the turtle a long turn.

activities.title: My Rule, Your Rule
activities.blurb: Good for a bossy kid and a parent who does not mind being bossed from a chair.
steps: Make one rule, like every time I clap you hop, and play it for a minute.
Then your kid makes the rule, and you both follow theirs.
For the last round keep both rules at once.

activities.title: Sock Money Shop
